## Description

Issue body actions

## Problem

A `SIZE_THAT_FITS` full-snapshot emission (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §"SizeThatFits") renders **every** candidate so CSS can gate the first paint (issue [#141](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/141)). When two candidates share a child `View`, that subtree is materialized **once per candidate**.

`assignIds` gives each node a unique sequential id, so ordinary nodes are unique — but any pass that **overrides an id after `assignIds`** (e.g. the media controller's pinned id) can reintroduce a duplicate. The resulting SSR then carries two nodes with the same `data-pathland-id`.

The DOM client keeps an `id → element` map, so a duplicate collapses to one entry; after the snapshot→live downgrade removes one candidate, deltas for that id land on a **removed** element. This silently breaks any id-keyed consumer (`PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_*`, …).

## Root cause

No spec invariant says "a frame's node ids are unique", and no emitter guard enforces it — so a duplicate id corrupts every id-keyed consumer without failing loudly.

## Spec changes (first)

1.  **`spec/OPCODE.md` §Frame Lifecycle** — add the invariant:
    
    > A frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id. `TREE` / `PARAMETER` opcodes reference each node id for exactly one node.
    
2.  **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §SizeThatFits** — document that in a full-snapshot emission a subtree shared between candidates is materialized **once per candidate**, and **every copy receives a distinct id** — no id is reused between candidates, including identity-stable nodes (e.g. a media controller).
    

## Implementation

1.  Make `assignIds` / `nextFreeId` the **single** id authority in the emitter (`pathland-view`'s `Emitter`).
2.  Add a **no-duplicate-id guard**: a tree/frame scan helper used by tests (and a `debug_assert` on emission) that fails loudly when two nodes share an id.
3.  Tests: a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` snapshot whose candidates share a subtree asserts unique ids across the whole frame — with and without a media controller.

## Acceptance

-   The unique-id invariant is in the spec.
-   The emitter fails loudly on a duplicate id (a test demonstrates the current controller pinning trips it).
-   The affected `status.md` files are updated.

## Branch hygiene

The current `spec/media-controller` branch is messy (interleaved commits, partially reverted fixes). Start this from `main` on a fresh branch (e.g. `fix/size-that-fits-unique-ids`).

1: # Pathland Primitive Views
2: 
3: **Wire protocol version:** 1
4: **Status:** Draft
5: **Last Updated:** October 15, 2026
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## Introduction
10: 
11: This document is the **semantic catalog of primitive nodes** the Pathland
12: protocol supports, organized by the three structural categories that drive
13: rendering. The **server** (the application/engine) dictates *what* the UI is —
14: structure, content, and intent. The **client platform renderer** measures
15: layout geometry, handles font/image assets, and maps each node onto that
16: platform's native elements, delegating interaction to native OS controls
17: wherever possible.
18: 
19: Every primitive maps to a protocol component type (`TREE::CREATE_NODE`), the
20: modifiers that shape it ([MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)), and the core events it
21: can produce ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)). This file is **implementation-ready**: a
22: renderer (GTK, HTML/SSR, or a new backend) can be written from
23: these tables alone. The wire encoding rules live in
24: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md); this file does not repeat them.
25: 
26: ### Structural categories
27: 
28: The protocol splits all supported nodes into three structural categories (the
29: component ID ranges are definitive — see [Definitive Opcode
30: Mapping Range](#definitive-opcode-mapping-range)):
31: 
32: | Range | Category | Behavior |
33: |-------|----------|----------|
34: | `0x01`–`0x0F` | **Primitive Drawing Nodes** | Low-level, non-decomposable building blocks (`Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`). The server dictates exact visual content and structural properties. The client measures layout geometry, handles font/image assets, and paints native elements. They hold **no independent interaction state machines**. |
35: | `0x10`–`0x1F` | **Layout & Container Primitives** | Structural arrangement (`VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, lazy grids/stacks). They arrange children and own scroll/virtualization; they carry no interaction semantics beyond scrolling. |
36: | `0x20`–`0x2F` | **Semantic Control Nodes** | High-order interaction and input controls (`Button`, `TextField`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `Picker`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`, `Menu`). They encapsulate intent, two-way bindings (`BINDING_ID`), accessibility traits, and local interaction physics (e.g. 120 FPS client-side thumb dragging). |
37: 
38: ### Relationship to other specs
39: 
40: | File | Role |
41: |------|------|
42: | [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format: categories, commands, 16-byte opcode layout, ring/arena, value types |
43: | **PRIMITIVES.md** (this file) | Which **views/nodes** exist and their protocol IDs |
44: | [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | Which **modifiers** (protocol properties) exist and how they encode |
45: | [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Which **core events** (raw inputs) exist and how they encode |
46: | [PROXY.md](./PROXY.md) | How a **proxy view** composes a subtree served by another Pathland server |
47: | [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden byte vectors |
48: 
49: > **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
50: > in each protocol crate/library — `pathland-core`, `pathland-render-gtk`,
51: > `pathland-render-html`, the Java libraries), **not** in
52: > this specification. This document defines the protocol contract only.
53: 
54: > **Enum-valued properties** (marked `ENUM` in the tables below) are carried on
55: > the wire with the `F32` value type, holding the numeric enum code as an f32
56: > bit pattern (see [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#value-types)). The codes are listed
57: > in [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values).
58: 
59: ### Non-negotiables (recap)
60: 
61: - Views are **declarative structure + constraint properties**, never positions.
62:   The engine emits `WHAT` (VStack, HStack, Text, …), never `WHERE`.
63: - Renderers are **stateless**: they map the opcode stream onto native elements
64:   and lay those elements out with their native layout engine. A renderer MAY
65:   retain its rendered-output tree for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing —
66:   this is a cache of its own output, not application state.
67: - **Native elements everywhere**: each primitive maps to the platform's native
68:   element (a stack → the platform's native stack; text → the platform's native
69:   text element); semantic controls → native OS controls in Native Token Mode
70:   (below). Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## Architectural Rules
75: 
76: ### 1. Core Structural Classification
77: 
78: Each node belongs to exactly one of the three categories above. The category
79: determines renderer responsibilities:
80: 
81: - **Primitive Drawing Nodes** hold no interaction state. The server sends the
82:   full visual description; the renderer measures and paints. If a primitive has
83:   no native equivalent (e.g. `Path`), the renderer may paint it directly — this
84:   is the one case where canvas-style painting is permitted.
85: - **Semantic Control Nodes** carry intent + two-way bindings (`BINDING_ID`),
86:   accessibility traits, and local interaction physics. Their *visual chrome* is
87:   delegated per the Dual-Mode rules below; their *interaction semantics* are
88:   always renderer-owned and reported as raw events.
89: 
90: ### 2. Dual-Mode Rendering Pipeline & Platform Delegation
91: 
92: Every semantic control node renders in **one of two modes**, decided by whether
93: the node has a child layout tree:
94: 
95: #### Native Token Mode (Leaf Control)
96: 
97: When a semantic control node has **no child layout tree** (`childrenIds` is
98: empty), the client platform **MUST delegate rendering entirely to its native OS
99: control** — `Button`, `TextField`/`SecureField`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
100: `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`, `Picker`, and `Menu` each map to the platform's
101: native control (the concrete widget per renderer lives in that renderer's
102: `status.md`).
103: 
104: **System style modifiers act as visual style tokens** — they force the platform
105: to switch native control variants **without emitting child nodes over the
106: wire**. Example: `TOGGLE_STYLE = CHECKBOX` renders `Toggle` (0x24) as a native
107: checkbox; `TOGGLE_STYLE = SWITCH` (default) as a native switch; `TOGGLE_STYLE =
108: BUTTON` as a toggle button.
109: 
110: #### Composite Override Mode (Container Control)
111: 
112: When a semantic control **contains child nodes** (or a custom style body is
113: defined on the server), the client platform **MUST**:
114: 
115: 1. **Suppress** its default native control visuals (the OS control chrome).
116: 2. **Render the custom view tree** sent by the server (the composite body).
117: 3. **Wrap that layout tree** with the native touch/click gestures, focus
118:    states, and event handlers that give the control its semantics.
119: 
120: The control keeps its interaction semantics (events, two-way bindings,
121: accessibility) even though its chrome is custom. Example: a `Button` with an
122: `HStack` child (icon + text) renders the `HStack` and wraps it with a native
123: click/press gesture that emits the button's events.
124: 
125: #### Leaf Property Fallbacks
126: 
127: If a control (e.g. `Button` 0x20) arrives with an **empty `childrenIds` list**,
128: renderers **MUST** check for direct string properties (the node's text content
129: set via `SET_TEXT`, or the `LABEL` 0x200A property for controls that define one)
130: before falling back to rendering an empty platform control shell. An empty shell
131: is a last resort, never the primary path.
132: 
133: ### 3. Transport-Aware Event Guards
134: 
135: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. User
136: interactions — taps, text changes, drags, value edits — **MUST NEVER** emit
137: outbound event opcodes unless the target node explicitly declared intent:
138: 
139: - it set the relevant `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
140: - it is a value-bearing control reporting by component type (see
141:   [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)), **or**
142: - it carries a bound callback property: `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
143:   (0x2017).
144: 
145: An interaction that matches none of these is dropped at the renderer — it is
146: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch.
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## Definitive Opcode Mapping Range
151: 
152: Component types are `u16` in `TREE::CREATE_NODE`. The ranges below are aligned
153: with SwiftUI's view categories and are the **single authoritative allocation**.
154: 
155: ### A. Primitive Drawing & Visual Nodes (`0x01`–`0x0F`)
156: 
157: | ID | Component | Notes |
158: | ---- | ----------- | ------- |
159: | `0x01` | `TEXT` | Standard styled text display |
160: | `0x02` | `IMAGE` | Raster, vector, or system icon asset (SF Symbols, material icons) |
161: | `0x03` | `COLOR` | Solid color / layout-filling background view (new node; formerly a property value only) |
162: | `0x04` | `SHAPE` | Vector geometries via `SHAPE_KIND` (`Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Capsule`, `Path`, …) |
163: | `0x05` | `DIVIDER` | Axis-aligned separator line |
164: | `0x06` | `SPACER` | Flexible expanding layout filler |
165: | `0x07` | `PROGRESS_VIEW` | Activity indicator / determinate progress |
166: | `0x08` | `GAUGE` | Range meter against a scale |
167: | `0x0A` | `VIDEO` | Video playback surface — renders a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER`'s video output (`MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`) |
168: | `0x0B` | `ICON` | Renderer-native symbol for a canonical name (`ICON_NAME`, spec/ICONS.md) |
169: | `0x0C`–`0x0F` | — | Future drawing/visual nodes |
170: 
171: ### B. Layout & Container Primitives (`0x10`–`0x1F`)
172: 
173: | ID | Component | Notes |
174: | ---- | ----------- | ------- |
175: | `0x10` | `VSTACK` | Vertical flex stack layout |
176: | `0x11` | `HSTACK` | Horizontal flex stack layout |
177: | `0x12` | `ZSTACK` | Depth-overlapping layer stack layout |
178: | `0x13` | `GRID` | Static 2D matrix grid (eagerly rendered, aligned rows & columns) |
179: | `0x14` | `SCROLLVIEW` | Scrollable content container |
180: | `0x15` | `LAZY_VGRID` | Virtualized vertical grid container (windowed rendering for large datasets) |
181: | `0x16` | `LAZY_HGRID` | Virtualized horizontal grid container |
182: | `0x17` | `SIZE_THAT_FITS` | **Fit slot** — renders its single (currently-selected) child; the renderer measures its own allocated width against the `FIT_QUERY` threshold list and only the selected child is transmitted (see below) |
183: | `0x18`–`0x1A` | — | Formerly `List`/`NavigationStack`/`NavigationSplitView` (composites, removed) — never reused |
184: | `0x1B` | `LAZY_VSTACK` | Virtualized vertical stack |
185: | `0x1C` | `LAZY_HSTACK` | Virtualized horizontal stack |
186: | `0x1D` | `GRID_ROW` | Explicit row grouping for `GRID` (planned): a grid child whose children are one row's cells — the SwiftUI `GridRow` authoring surface |
187: | `0x1E` | `PROXY_VIEW` | **Proxy view** — a transparent single-child container whose child subtree is served by **another** Pathland server; the proxying server remaps the foreign subtree's node ids into a disjoint high range and routes its events back to the origin (see [PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) |
188: | `0x1F` | — | Future layout/container nodes |
189: 
190: ### C. Semantic Control Nodes (`0x20`–`0x2F`)
191: 
192: | ID | Component | Notes |
193: | ---- | ----------- | ------- |
194: | `0x20` | `BUTTON` | Action trigger control |
195: | `0x21` | `TEXT_FIELD` / `SECURE_FIELD` | Single-line text input (`IS_SECURE` token for secure variant) |
196: | `0x22` | `TEXT_EDITOR` | Multi-line text editing area (new) |
197: | `0x23` | — | Future semantic control |
198: | `0x24` | `TOGGLE` | Boolean switch, checkbox, or button control (`TOGGLE_STYLE`) |
199: | `0x25` | `SLIDER` | Continuous or stepped numeric range control |
200: | `0x26` | `STEPPER` | Discrete increment/decrement control |
201: | `0x27` | `DATE_PICKER` | Date & time selection modal/popover control |
202: | `0x28` | `PICKER` | Selection control (segment, dropdown menu, or wheel) |
203: | `0x29` | `MENU` | Contextual action trigger + popover container |
204: | `0x2A` | `COLOR_PICKER` | Native system color picker control |
205: | `0x2B`–`0x2F` | — | Future semantic controls |
206: 
207: ### D. Non-visual / resource nodes (`0x30`–`0x3F`)
208: 
209: Nodes that exist in the retained tree but are **layout-transparent** and render
210: **no** native element. They carry a resource or a control surface for other
211: nodes to reference.
212: 
213: | ID | Component | Notes |
214: | ---- | ----------- | ------- |
215: | `0x30` | `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` | **Media controller** — a non-visual node that owns a media resource and its transport state; a `VIDEO` surface references it (see [MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)) |
216: | `0x31`–`0x3F` | — | Future non-visual/resource nodes |
217: 
218: ### Utility & custom
219: 
220: | ID | Component | Notes |
221: | ---- | ----------- | ------- |
222: | `0x7F` | `COMMENT` | Opaque/debug node; renderers ignore it (no native element) |
223: | `0x0100`–`0xFFFF` | — | Application/custom component types |
224: 
225: ### Composite views (not primitives)
226: 
227: These SwiftUI views are **not** protocol primitives. Applications compose them
228: from the primitives in this file, so no component IDs are allocated:
229: 
230: | SwiftUI view | Composition |
231: |--------------|-------------|
232: | `List` | `ScrollView` + `VStack` of rows; row selection via `SELECTED` per row |
233: | `NavigationStack` | app-held navigation state emitting the current destination into a stable `Group` slot (a structural container, [DSL.md §3.4](./DSL.md#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)); the slot's child swaps on route change, producing `TREE` deltas |
234: | `NavigationSplitView` | `HStack` (sidebar + detail) |
235: | `Label` | `HStack` + `IMAGE` (or `ICON`) + `TEXT` |

238: 
239: ## A. Primitive Drawing & Visual Nodes
240: 
241: ### Text — `TEXT` 0x01
242: 
243: A run of styled text. The server dictates content and style; the client measures
244: and renders.
245: 
246: - **Protocol**: a leaf node; content via `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT` or a bound signal.
247: - **Properties**: `LINE_LIMIT` (0x000B, U32), `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` (0x000C, enum
248:   code), `TRUNCATION_MODE` (0x000D, enum code), plus all text-formatting and
249:   appearance modifiers from [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md).
250: - **Content fitting**: an unconstrained Text is a single line at its natural
251:   width; a constrained width (Fixed `WIDTH`) wraps at word boundaries;
252:   `LINE_LIMIT` clamps the line count with a tail ellipsis; `TRUNCATION_MODE`
253:   positions that ellipsis under a clamp; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips the Text to its
254:   bounds box. Full contract: [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md#content-fitting-truncation--clipping).
255: - **Events**: none by default; any listener via `EVENT_LISTENERS`.
256: - **Font handling**: client-owned — the renderer resolves `FONT_FAMILY` /
257:   `FONT_*` to its native text system.
258: 
259: ### Image — `IMAGE` 0x02
260: 
261: A static image or icon asset. Asset loading is client-owned.
262: 
263: - **Protocol**: a leaf node; source via `IMAGE_SOURCE` (0x1002, STRING: a
264:   resource name, file path, or absolute URL).
265: - **Properties**: `IMAGE_SOURCE`, `CONTENT_MODE` (0x001C, enum `Fit`=0 /
266:   `Fill`=1), size modifiers, `OPACITY`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`.
267: - **Events**: none by default.
268: - **Note (SwiftUI `AsyncImage`)**: remote/async loading is **not a separate
269:   primitive** — it is `IMAGE` with `IMAGE_SOURCE` set to an absolute URL; the
270:   renderer loads asynchronously and re-issues `SET_PROPERTY(IMAGE_SOURCE)` if
271:   the source changes.
272: 
273: ### Icon — `ICON` 0x0B
274: 
275: A **renderer-native symbol** for a canonical semantic name — unlike `IMAGE`,
276: which loads an asset, an icon is a *word* the renderer maps onto its native
277: icon set (spec/ICONS.md).
278: 
279: - **Protocol**: a leaf node; the symbol via `ICON_NAME` (0x1038, STRING: the
280:   canonical name). The application owns the intent; the renderer owns the glyph.
281: - **Properties**: `ICON_NAME`, `COLOR`/`foregroundStyle` (tint), `FONT_SIZE`
282:   (size — after SwiftUI's font-based symbol sizing), size modifiers,
283:   `OPACITY`, `LABEL` (accessibility).
284: - **Events**: none by default.
285: - **Fallback**: an unknown canonical name (a name the vocabulary has not
286:   allocated) resolves to a renderer-owned placeholder (spec/ICONS.md).
287: 
288: ### Video — `VIDEO` 0x0A
289: 
290: A **video media surface**: a view that references a
291: [`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`](#media-controller--media_controller-0x30) and renders that
292: playback's **video output** in its own box. It owns the box, the content mode,
293: and the controls; the playback belongs to the controller ([MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)).
294: (Audio has no view of its own — an audio playback is a controller plus the
295: application's own control views, [MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md).)
296: 
297: - **Protocol**: a leaf node by default; references its playback with
298:   `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A) and carries **no source of its own** (the source
299:   lives on the controller as `MEDIA_SOURCE`). A custom `VideoStyle` supplies
300:   app-driven control children.
301: - **Properties**: `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`, `CONTENT_MODE` (`Fit`/`Fill`), size and
302:   style modifiers.
303: - **Events**: none on the surface; the `MEDIA_*` family reports against the
304:   **controller** id.
305: - **Note**: a poster/preview frame is a planned draft (`POSTER_SOURCE`, on the
306:   surface); a video plays fine without one.
307: 
308: ### Media Controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30
309: 
310: A **media controller**: a **non-visual** node that owns a media resource and its
311: transport state, so playback survives structural changes and can be controlled
312: from several places at once. A `VIDEO` surface **references** it by id
313: (`MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`) — the relationship is a reference, not a parent/child
314: edge; a controller has no children of its own. An audio playback is a controller
315: with **no** media view, controlled by the application's own views.
316: 
317: - **Protocol**: a leaf node carrying `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B, STRING asset
318:   reference) and the transport commands — `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035, U32 0/1),
319:   `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036, F32 seconds; a change seeks), `MEDIA_VOLUME`
320:   (0x1037, F32 0..1), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C, U8), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D, U8),
321:   `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E, F32). It is created/deleted like any node, so it
322:   participates in the structural diff, full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and
323:   proxy-id remapping with no media-specific machinery.
324: - **Layout**: **layout-transparent** — no native element, no box, no space, no
325:   spacing contribution (like `COMMENT` and the `PROXY_VIEW` passthrough,
326:   [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md)). Place it for **lifetime stability** (outside any
327:   swapping branch such as a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot), not for layout.
328: - **Events**: the `MEDIA_*` family targets the controller id, gated by the
329:   transport properties bound on it (see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#media)).
330: - **Independence**: attaching/detaching a `VIDEO` surface never starts, stops,
331:   seeks, or re-loads playback; a controller with zero media views keeps playing.
332:   One controller = one playback, shared by every surface that references it.
333: - **Kind**: kind-agnostic. A controller referenced by a `VIDEO` surface renders
334:   video; otherwise the playback is audio (presented by the application's own
335:   views, never by the protocol).
336: 
337: The full contract — the model, the swap rules, the guards, and the renderer
338: obligations — is specified in [MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md).
339: 
340: ### Color — `COLOR` 0x03
341: 
342: `Color` mirrors SwiftUI's **dual identity**: it is both a **View** and a
343: **Data Type** — and it is **never a modifier**.
344: 
345: - **As a View**: a solid-color visual element. It is **layout-greedy** —
346:   it expands to fill all available space offered by its parent container
347:   unless explicitly constrained (e.g. by a `.frame`/size modifier). Its color
348:   is the `COLOR` property (0x100A, packed `0xAARRGGBB`, sRGB).
349: - **As a Data Type**: a `Color` value is passed *into* style-taking modifiers
350:   (`.foregroundStyle(_:)`, `.background(_:)`, `.border(_:)`, `.tint(_:)`), and
351:   can be used anywhere a visual fill/style is expected.
352: - **Constraint**: there is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)`
353:   is deprecated — all foreground styling uses `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
354: - **Parser/generator rule**: treat `Color` as a **View** when it is a structural
355:   node in the UI tree; treat it as a **Value** when it appears in a modifier's
356:   parameter list.
357: - **Events**: none by default.
358: - **Note**: `Color` is also a **property value** (`COLOR`,
359:   `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `BORDER_COLOR`, `TINT`) — the node exists for when a
360:   color is a first-class view (backgrounds, fills, spacers).
361: 
362: ### Shape — `SHAPE` 0x04
363: 
364: A vector geometry. The shape kind is data (`SHAPE_KIND`), never a visual rule —
365: the renderer owns the actual drawing.
366: 
367: - **Protocol**: a leaf node with `SHAPE_KIND` (0x0006, enum): `Circle`=0,
368:   `Rectangle`=1, `RoundedRectangle`=2, `Capsule`=3, `Ellipse`=4, `Path`=5.
369: - **Properties**: fill = `COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`; stroke = `BORDER_WIDTH`,
370:   `BORDER_COLOR`, `BORDER_RADIUS` (RoundedRectangle corner), `BORDER_EDGES`;
371:   size = `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`.
372: - **Events**: none by default.
373: 
374: ### Divider — `DIVIDER` 0x05
375: 
376: An axis-aligned 1px separator line.
377: 
378: - **Protocol**: a leaf node; orientation implied by the parent stack axis.
379: - **Properties**: `COLOR` (0x100A), `BORDER_WIDTH` (0x1003) — line thickness.
380: - **Events**: none.
381: - **Layout-greedy on the cross axis** (fills the stack's available cross size,
382:   SwiftUI-style) — see LAYOUT.md; an explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides it.
383: 
384: ### Spacer — `SPACER` 0x06
385: 
386: A flexible expanding layout filler.
387: 
388: - **Protocol**: a leaf node with no properties; expands to the remaining main
389:   axis space.
390: - **Events**: none.
391: 
392: ### ProgressView — `PROGRESS_VIEW` 0x07
393: 
394: Determinate progress or an activity indicator.
395: 
396: - **Protocol**: a leaf node. Determinate: `PROGRESS` (0x200E, F32 0.0–1.0, or
397:   0.0–`MAX_VALUE` if set). Indeterminate: `IS_INDETERMINATE` (0x200F, U8 1) —
398:   the renderer animates a native activity indicator.
399: - **Events**: none.
400: 
401: ### Gauge — `GAUGE` 0x08
402: 
403: A value shown against a scale (SwiftUI `Gauge`).
404: 
405: - **Protocol**: a leaf node with `VALUE` (0x2006), `MIN_VALUE` (0x2007),
406:   `MAX_VALUE` (0x2008). The gauge style (linear/circular) is renderer/token-owned.
407: - **Events**: none (read-only; an interactive gauge is a `Slider` 0x25).
408:

411: ## B. Layout & Container Primitives
412: 
413: Layout primitives arrange children. They carry `SPACING` (0x0001),
414: `ALIGNMENT` (0x0002), and `CONTENT_MARGINS` (0x0005), plus layout modifiers from
415: [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#1-layout). Renderers map them to their native
416: layout primitives.
417: 
418: ### The stack layout model
419: 
420: `VStack`/`HStack` (and the lazy stacks) follow the **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose
421: layout model**: a stack *proposes* a size to each child, the child reports its
422: own size, and the stack *places* it. The protocol transmits **intent** — size
423: kinds and alignment — never geometry; the renderer resolves the proposal with
424: its native layout engine. The full allocation contract is
425: [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md); the essentials:
426: 
427: **Size kinds.** Each `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` is one of three kinds (LAYOUT.md §size
428: model):
429: 
430: | Kind | Wire value | Meaning |
431: |------|-----------|---------|
432: | **Fixed** | finite `F32` | exactly that many points |
433: | **Fill** | `-1` | expand to available space |
434: | **Hug** | `-2` / absent | natural size |
435: 
436: **Main vs cross axis.** The **main axis** is the stack's layout direction
437: (VStack = vertical, HStack = horizontal); the other is the **cross axis**.
438: 
439: **Main-axis allocation.** A child is Fixed (exact box), Fill (expands), or Hug
440: (natural). **Leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill` children** (and to
441: `Spacer`, which is Fill by nature); a stack with no Fill child leaves the
442: leftover empty at the end. Every other child is packed from the start.
443: 
444: **Cross-axis allocation.** A child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
445: **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` — position-only, it never resizes. A stack reads a
446: **single axis** of the 2D position code (see the [ZStack alignment
447: table](#zstack--zstack-0x12)): a `VStack` reads the horizontal component
448: (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), an `HStack` the vertical (`0/1/2` =
449: top/center/bottom). The default is the start position (Compose `Column` defaults
450: `Alignment.Start`, `Row` defaults `Alignment.Top`; SwiftUI's stack default is
451: `.center` — a per-framework difference, all three are expressible with an
452: explicit `ALIGNMENT`). Only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's
453: cross size.
454: 
455: **Fill propagation.** A Hug-sized stack that contains a **`Fill`-sized child or
456: `Spacer` on an axis is itself `Fill`-sized on that axis** — the child's
457: expansion propagates to the stack, which then fills its parent's proposal on
458: that axis. This matches both reference frameworks:
459: 
460: - SwiftUI `VStack { Button().frame(maxWidth: .infinity) }` fills the width.
461: - Compose `Column { Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) }` fills the width.
462: - `VStack { Spacer() }` fills the proposed height.
463: 
464: A full-width row is therefore expressed as a `Fill`-width child (or `Spacer`)
465: inside the stack, never by stretching the stack itself.
466: 
467: **Spacing.** `SPACING` is a fixed gap between **adjacent** children (never
468: before the first or after the last), clamped to ≥ 0. It matches SwiftUI
469: `VStack(spacing:)` and Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy(...)`. Leftover space is
470: distributed by `Fill` children / `Spacer`, never by the gap.
471: 
472: **Insets.** `CONTENT_MARGINS` is the stack's uniform content inset
473: (equivalently, `PADDING` on the stack). Both compose; when both are present on
474: the same node, precedence is per-edge `PADDING_*` > `PADDING` >
475: `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
476: 
477: **Overflow.** A Fixed box **constrains layout but does not clip**: content that
478: exceeds the box is drawn outside it unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI
479: `.clipped()` parity). A stack inside a `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls instead.
480: 
481: ### VStack — `VSTACK` 0x10
482: 
483: Vertical flex stack. **Properties**: `SPACING`, `ALIGNMENT` (enum: `Leading`=0,
484: `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
485: 
486: **Layout & sizing**
487: 
488: - **Main axis (vertical)**: children are allocated per the stack model —
489:   Fixed exact, Fill expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A
490:   Hug VStack's height is the sum of its children's heights plus `SPACING`
491:   between them.
492: - **Cross axis (horizontal)**: children keep their own width (a Fixed box, or a
493:   Hug natural width); `Fill`-width children stretch to the stack's width. Narrow
494:   children are positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default Leading/Start).
495: - **Own size**: Hug by default (height = content + spacing; width = widest
496:   child). A Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
497:   propagation — expands to the parent's proposal. A `Fill`-width child makes
498:   the stack full-width; a `Fill`-height child makes it full-height.
499: - **Edge cases**: negative `SPACING` → 0; no Fill child + leftover → empty at
500:   the end; a Fixed-width child narrower than the stack keeps its exact box and
501:   is aligned; a `Fill` child in a Hug stack propagates (fills the parent's
502:   proposal); root stacks are typically `Fill`
503:   (`.modifiers(frame(f -> f.width(FILL).height(FILL)))`).
504: 
505: ### HStack — `HSTACK` 0x11
506: 
507: Horizontal flex stack. Same properties as `VStack`, mirrored:
508: 
509: - **Main axis (horizontal)**: children per the stack model — Fixed exact, Fill
510:   expands (leftover only to `Fill`/`Spacer`), Hug natural. A Hug HStack's width
511:   is the sum of its children's widths plus `SPACING`.
512: - **Cross axis (vertical)**: children keep their own height (Fixed or Hug);
513:   `Fill`-height children stretch. Positioned per `ALIGNMENT` (default
514:   Leading/Start; Compose `Row` defaults to `Top`, SwiftUI's HStack to `.center`).
515: - **Own size**: Hug by default (width = content + spacing; height = tallest
516:   child); a Fixed box exact; `Fill`/propagation expands.
517: - **Edge cases**: as VStack.
518: 
519: ### ZStack — `ZSTACK` 0x12
520: 
521: Depth-overlapping layer stack: children are drawn in depth order — **child index =
522: draw order**, later = on top. An explicit `Z_INDEX` overrides that order: a
523: higher value draws **on top of** lower values, and equal values tie-break by
524: child index (SwiftUI `.zIndex(_:)` parity). **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (enum:
525: `Leading`=0, `Center`=1, `Trailing`=2, `Fill`=3), plus layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill
526: `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `PADDING`, `CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset). **No `SPACING`** —
527: children occupy the same box by design; there is no gap between them.
528: 
529: **Layout & sizing** (SwiftUI `ZStack` / Compose `Box` semantics)
530: 
531: - **Overlay allocation**: unlike a flex stack, children do **not** add to each
532:   other along an axis — they share one box. Each child keeps its own size (a
533:   Fixed box, or a Hug natural size) and is **positioned** by `ALIGNMENT` on
534:   **both axes**; only a **`Fill`-sized child** stretches to the stack's size.
535: - **Own size**: the stack **hugs to its largest child** by default — on each
536:   axis its size is the **maximum** of its children's sizes, never the sum. A
537:   Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` makes the box exact; a `Fill` axis — or fill
538:   propagation (a `Fill` child on an axis makes the Hug stack `Fill` on that
539:   axis, see the stack layout model above) — expands to the parent's proposal.
540:   `ZStack { Color.red }` fills (Color is layout-greedy); `ZStack { Text("hi") }`
541:   hugs the text.
542: - **Alignment**: `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on **both** axes with a
543:   **2D position code** (SwiftUI `Alignment` / Compose `Alignment` parity) — the
544:   code's horizontal and vertical components place the child within the stack's
545:   box. Position-only: it never resizes a child.
546: 
547:   | code | horizontal | vertical | meaning |
548:   |------|------------|----------|---------|
549:   | `0` | start | start | top-leading |
550:   | `1` | center | center | centered |
551:   | `2` | end | end | bottom-trailing |
552:   | `3` | center | start | top-center |
553:   | `4` | center | end | bottom-center |
554:   | `5` | start | center | center-leading |
555:   | `6` | end | center | center-trailing |
556:   | `7` | end | start | top-trailing |
557:   | `8` | start | end | bottom-leading |
558: 
559:   `0`/absent is the default (top-leading, Compose `TopStart` parity; SwiftUI
560:   `ZStack` defaults to `.center`). A **stack** (`VStack`/`HStack`) reads a
561:   **single axis** of the same code — the `VStack` cross-axis is horizontal
562:   (`0/1/2` = leading/center/trailing), the `HStack` cross-axis vertical
563:   (`0/1/2` = top/center/bottom).
564: - **Overflow**: a Fixed box constrains layout but does not clip — content that
565:   exceeds it is drawn outside the box unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it
566:   (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity).
567: - **Edge cases**: the first child is **not** a special "background" — it follows
568:   the same size model (a Fixed first child keeps its exact box; a `Fill` one
569:   stretches); draw order is child index, with an explicit `Z_INDEX` overriding it
570:   (higher = on top, equal → child index); a `Fill` child in a Hug ZStack
571:   propagates (fills the parent's proposal).
572: 
573: ### Grid — `GRID` 0x13
574: 
575: Static 2D matrix grid, eagerly rendered with aligned rows & columns. Children
576: are cells, **row-major in insertion order** — child *i* occupies the cell at
577: `(row = i / columns, column = i % columns)`. **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (a 2D
578: position code applied per-cell, like `ZStack` — the [ZStack alignment
579: table](#zstack--zstack-0x12)), `SPACING`
580: (uniform row + column gap), `GRID_COLUMNS` (column count), `GRID_ROWS` (row
581: count), plus layout modifiers (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frames — the grid's box, never a
582: count — `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset).
583: 
584: #### The grid layout model
585: 
586: `GRID` (and the lazy grids) follow the **SwiftUI / Jetpack Compose grid model**:
587: a grid *proposes* a size to each cell, the cell reports its own size, and the
588: grid *places* it at its track intersection. Unlike a stack, a grid has no main
589: axis — its two track axes (columns × rows) follow the size model
590: [above](#the-stack-layout-model) independently, with two differences:
591: 
592: **Cell counts.** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) is the **column count** and
593: `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`) the **row count**. A **Fixed** value pins that count;
594: **`FILL` or absent means auto-fit** — the grid derives the count from the number
595: of cells and the available space (Compose `GridCells.Fixed(N)` vs `Adaptive`;
596: SwiftUI `LazyVGrid(columns:)` / `LazyHGrid(rows:)`). They are **constructor
597: properties** (never chainable modifiers) and are **never pixel sizes**.
598: 
599: **Tracks.** On a **fixed-count** axis the tracks are **equal `1fr` fractions**
600: of the grid's size on that axis (`repeat(N, 1fr)` in CSS, Compose
601: `GridCells.Fixed`, SwiftUI `.flexible()` columns): every track gets the same
602: share. A Hug grid on that axis sizes the tracks to the content instead (each
603: track as large as its widest/tallest cell) and hugs to the content + `SPACING`.
604: The **auto** axis always sizes tracks to the content — each row/column is
605: exactly as large as its cells need.
606: 
607: **Per-track sizes (`GRID_TRACKS`).** For per-track control a grid may carry a
608: **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) constructor property — a comma-separated
609: track list, one entry per track on the fixed-count axis, **taking precedence**
610: over `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` (a bare count is the `N`×`flexible` sugar). Each
611: entry is:
612: 
613: | Token | Meaning | CSS | Compose | SwiftUI |
614: |-------|---------|-----|---------|---------|
615: | `flex` | equal `1fr` share (the count's track) | `1fr` | `GridCells.Fixed` column | `.flexible()` |
616: | `fixed:<points>` | exactly `<points>` wide | `<points>px` | fixed dp column | `.fixed(_:)` |
617: | `adaptive:<points>` | auto-fit, at least `<points>` (fit as many as fit) | `minmax(<points>px,1fr)` | `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize)` | `.adaptive(minimum:)` |
618: 
619: The track list is **CSS-grid-native** — renderers whose native grid has no
620: per-track sizing equivalent (GTK `GtkGrid`) size tracks naturally instead
621: (renderer status, not a protocol contract).
622: 
623: **Spacing.** `SPACING` is a **uniform gap between tracks on both axes** — the
624: row gap and the column gap are the same value (Compose `Arrangement.spacedBy`,
625: CSS `gap`), clamped to ≥ 0, never before the first or after the last track.
626: 
627: **Per-cell allocation.** Each cell keeps its own size on both axes (a Fixed box,
628: or Hug content) and is **positioned** within its track by the grid's `ALIGNMENT`
629: (a **2D position code**, like `ZStack` — the [table
630: above](#zstack--zstack-0x12)) — e.g. `0`/absent = top-leading, `3` = top-center.
631: Position-only: it never resizes a cell. Only a **`Fill`-sized cell** (or a
632: greedy filler like `COLOR`) stretches to fill its track.
633: 
634: **Own size & edge cases.** A grid follows the universal size model: **Hug**
635: (content tracks + `SPACING`), a Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` **box**, or **`Fill`**
636: (expands to the parent's proposal). `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` never size the
637: grid — they only set the track counts. A grid **never propagates** a `Fill` cell
638: up to a Hug parent — a `Fill` cell fills its own track, and the grid's own size
639: comes from its own frame. Negative `SPACING` → 0; a Fixed box constrains layout
640: but does not clip (`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips).
641: 
642: ### GridRow — `GRID_ROW` 0x1D
643: 
644: An **explicit row grouping** for a `GRID` (the SwiftUI `GridRow` authoring
645: surface): a grid's children are **cells or `GRID_ROW`s**, and a `GRID_ROW`'s
646: children are the cells of **one row**. It lets the author control row layout
647: directly instead of relying on row-major index flow.
648: 
649: - **Row placement.** A `GRID_ROW` always starts a new row: its children are
650:   placed left-to-right in that row starting at column 0, then the row advances.
651:   **Bare cells** (direct `GRID` children) auto-flow row-major, advancing to the
652:   next row after `GRID_COLUMNS` cells (or auto, below).
653: - **Column count.** The equal-`1fr` track count is `GRID_COLUMNS` when set;
654:   otherwise the **widest row** (a `GRID_ROW` or a bare-cell run) defines it. A
655:   short row leaves its trailing columns **empty** — a cell never pulls the next
656:   row's cells forward.
657: - **Structure.** A `GRID_ROW` is structural only: it renders nothing outside a
658:   `GRID` (like `COMMENT`), and renderers flatten its cells into the grid's rows.
659:   Its own `ALIGNMENT`/`SPACING`/size properties are ignored.
660: - **Example.** `Grid { GridRow { A; B }; GridRow { C; D }; E }` lays out row 0 =
661:   `A B`, row 1 = `C D`, row 2 = `E` (auto-flowing to the next row after the two
662:   columns defined by the widest row).
663: 
664: ### ScrollView — `SCROLLVIEW` 0x14
665: 
666: A scrollable content container. **Layout-greedy on both axes** by default — it
667: fills the available space (SwiftUI `ScrollView` / Compose scroll semantics); an
668: explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides it (LAYOUT.md §layout-greedy primitives).
669: **Properties**: layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill frames, `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`
670: as an inset).
671: 
672: **Content.** The **first child** is the content; a scroll view carries a single
673: content subtree (typically a stack), matching SwiftUI/Compose's single-content
674: contract. The content is measured with an **unbounded proposal** on both axes —
675: it may grow beyond the viewport (that is what scrolls). The **viewport** is the
676: scroll view's allocated box; a Hug `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` — or a Hug parent proposal
677: on an axis — sizes the viewport to the content's natural size on that axis (the
678: viewport fits the content, so that axis does not scroll).
679: 
680: **Overflow.** A scroll view scrolls its content rather than clipping it — the
681: viewport clips by virtue of scrolling; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` on the scroll view has
682: no further effect on the content.
683: 
684: **Events.** With the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8) the renderer reports the
685: content offset in logical points via `EVENT::SCROLL`; with `WHEEL` (bit 9) it
686: reports wheel/trackpad deltas via `EVENT::WHEEL` (both draft — see
687: [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)).
688: 
689: ### LazyVGrid — `LAZY_VGRID` 0x15
690: 
691: Virtualized vertical grid. **Allocation is identical to `GRID`** — row-major
692: cells, `GRID_COLUMNS` = column count (Fixed pins it, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit),
693: equal `1fr` columns, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment, hug-to-content
694: own size. The only difference is **realization**: a renderer MAY defer realizing
695: off-screen cells until scrolled into view and MAY discard realized cells that
696: leave the viewport. Realization never changes layout — a cell's position is
697: always its row-major index in the full cell list. Typically nested inside a
698: `SCROLLVIEW`.
699: 
700: ### LazyHGrid — `LAZY_HGRID` 0x16
701: 
702: Virtualized horizontal grid; the flipped-axis form of `LAZY_VGRID`. **Allocation
703: is identical to `GRID` mirrored**: cells are **column-major** in insertion
704: order, `GRID_ROWS` = row count (Fixed pins it, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit), equal
705: `1fr` rows, columns auto-flow, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment,
706: windowed realization.
707: 
708: ### LazyVStack — `LAZY_VSTACK` 0x1B
709: 
710: Virtualized vertical stack. **Allocation is identical to `VStack`** (the stack
711: layout model above — same properties, sizing, spacing, alignment, and fill
712: propagation); only **realization** differs: a renderer MAY defer realizing
713: children outside the visible region.
714: 
715: ### LazyHStack — `LAZY_HSTACK` 0x1C
716: 
717: Virtualized horizontal stack. **Allocation is identical to `HStack`**; only
718: realization is windowed.
719: 
720: ### SizeThatFits — `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17
721: 
722: A **fit slot**: it shows **one child at a time — the currently selected
723: candidate**. In the **live (delta) form** only that child is ever transmitted:
724: the app owns the candidates (their views never ride the wire) and transmits the
725: **fit query** (`FIT_QUERY`, LIST — the candidates' `minWidth` thresholds,
726: ascending) plus the selected child. In a **full-snapshot emission** (the web SSR
727: first document), every candidate is transmitted as a child — the renderer renders
728: all branches and the browser selects the matching one (see the visibility
729: contract below) so the first paint is already correct. The renderer measures its
730: **own allocated width** (the slot is size-taking — it stretches to its parent's
731: proposal, never hugs, so it always has a well-defined width) and selects the fit
732: **locally**:
733: 
734: > **Fit rule** — the selected index is `max{ i : thresholds[i] ≤ measured
735: > width }` (threshold 0 candidate always qualifies — the fallback); equal
736: > thresholds pick the **lower index**; before the first measure the app renders
737: > the threshold-0 candidate (index 0). The measurement is in **logical points**,
738: > so the pick is identical on every renderer given the same slot width.
739: 
740: The renderer reports its selection back with **`FIT_CHANGED`** ([EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md))
741: — emitted **once after the first measure, and then only when the derived fit
742: index changes** (a band crossing). It never streams the raw size. The app reacts
743: by swapping the slot's child (a `TREE` delta pair); a selection that maps to the
744: already-shown view re-emits **zero** opcodes. After a **full-snapshot**
745: presentation (all candidates laid out), the first `FIT_CHANGED` is the signal
746: that collapses the slot back to the live single-selected-child form.
747: 
748: **Candidate identity (MUST).** The candidate **index `i`** is the candidate's
749: position in the **ascending `FIT_QUERY` table** (equal thresholds keep the app's
750: surface order). In a **full-snapshot emission** the slot's **child order MUST
751: equal `FIT_QUERY` order** — the child at position `i` is candidate `i`. The fit
752: rule, the `FIT_CHANGED` payload, and the CSS gate all use this one mapping. A
753: candidate declared first in the DSL but carrying a **higher** `minWidth` is
754: therefore **not** index 0.
755: 
756: **Full-snapshot visibility (MUST).** In a full-snapshot emission the renderer
757: MUST show **exactly one** candidate — the one at `index(w)` for the slot's own
758: allocated width `w` — with no JS:
759: 
760: - the slot's own width is the query context (each slot is measured
761:   independently);
762: - each candidate is gated behind a marker carrying its `FIT_QUERY` index;
763: - for every threshold `T_i` with `i ≥ 1` there is a **band** that, at
764:   `w ≥ T_i`, makes candidate `i` visible and **hides every candidate `j ≠ i`**;
765:   bands are emitted **ascending** so the highest matching band wins; no band
766:   exists for `T_0`;
767: - the per-candidate **default** (below the first band / no match) is candidate
768:   `0` visible, every other candidate hidden;
769: - **invariant**: exactly one candidate is visible at every width.
770: 
771: **Hydration collapse (MUST).** After the first `FIT_CHANGED` the app swaps the
772: slot to the live single-selected-child form (the unselected candidates leave as
773: `TREE` deltas) and the renderer removes the full-snapshot gating — the gate
774: markers, the query context, and the band rules — so no CSS gate remains; a
775: `FIT_CHANGED` that maps to the already-shown candidate re-emits **zero** opcodes.
776: 
777: The collapse is signalled by the **removal of a candidate** (a `TREE` `REMOVE_CHILD`
778: /`DELETE_NODE` on the slot), not by an arbitrary structural op. A **full-snapshot
779: emission replayed as opcodes** (e.g. `META::RESYNC`) therefore does **not** collapse
780: the slot: the renderer reuses its existing gate (the SSR gate markers + band rules)
781: and keeps showing the width-correct candidate. The app's retained tree stays in the
782: snapshot form until the first `FIT_CHANGED` downgrade actually removes a candidate.
783: 
784: The concrete web realization (CSS container + per-candidate gate wrappers +
785: `@container` band rules) is **renderer-owned** and described in
786: `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/status.md`.
787: 
788: Semantics:
789: - **Properties**: `FIT_QUERY` (`0x1039`, LIST).
790: - **Events**: `FIT_CHANGED` (`0x13`, host → guest) — reported fit index.
791: - **Children**: at most one in the live form; all candidates in a
792:   full-snapshot emission (the web SSR's first document), in `FIT_QUERY` order.
793: - **Renderer statelessness**: the measured width and derived index are layout
794:   output, not retained application state.
795: 
796: ### ProxyView — `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E
797: 
798: A **proxy view**: a transparent container whose child subtree is served by a
799: **different Pathland server**. It lets one app compose views from several
800: servers into a single unified document. The proxying server (the app that owns
801: the proxy node) connects to the origin server as a Pathland **host** (client),
802: receives the origin's subtree, and splices it into its own stream.
803: 
804: - **Protocol**: a container node with **exactly one** child in the live form —
805:   the origin subtree's root. The origin subtree's nodes are ordinary nodes of
806:   the same protocol; the proxying server has **remapped their node ids** into a
807:   disjoint high range so they never collide with the proxying app's own ids.
808: - **Layout**: a **transparent passthrough** container. It imposes no spacing or
809:   alignment of its own; it proposes its own allocated size to its single child
810:   and, unless the app constrains it (`frame`/size modifiers), sizes to that
811:   child. Renderers render it as a plain container (a box/`div`) — there is no
812:   proxy-specific native element.
813: - **Events**: raw events whose target id falls in a proxy's remapped range are
814:   the origin server's; the proxying server forwards them (id remapped back) to
815:   the origin over the origin connection rather than dispatching them locally.
816: - **Ownership**: the proxy node belongs to the proxying app's retained tree; the
817:   child subtree belongs to the origin server's retained tree. The proxying app
818:   never diffs the origin subtree — it forwards the origin's deltas verbatim
819:   (id-remapped). A **full-snapshot** (`META::RESYNC`) of the proxying app embeds
820:   the origin's current snapshot; the origin snapshot is requested with a
821:   `META::RESYNC` sent to the origin server (there is no proxy-specific opcode).
822: - **Renderer statelessness**: a renderer applies the remapped origin opcodes
823:   like any other opcodes; it holds no notion of "remote".
824: 
825: The full contract — id namespacing, the snapshot/`RESYNC` handshake, event
826: routing, SSR embedding, and the backpressure policy — is specified in
827: [PROXY.md](./PROXY.md).
828: 
829: ---
830: 
831: ## C. Semantic Control Nodes
832: 
833: Semantic controls encapsulate intent, two-way bindings, accessibility traits,
834: and local interaction physics. Rendering follows the [Dual-Mode Rendering
835: Pipeline](#2-dual-mode-rendering-pipeline--platform-delegation): **Native Token
836: Mode** when the node has no children; **Composite Override Mode** when it does.
837: 
838: ### Button — `BUTTON` 0x20
839: 
840: An action trigger control.
841: 
842: | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
843: |----------|----|------|---------|
844: | label text | `SET_TEXT` / `TEXT` | STRING | The button's text label (leaf mode fallback) |
845: | `ACTION_ID` | 0x2016 | U32 | Callback id that gates event delivery (Event Guards) |
846: | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (bound to the action's value, if any) |
847: | `ENABLED` | 0x2003 | U8 | 1 = interactive, 0 = disabled |
848: | `STATE` | 0x2002 | F32 (enum) | Accessibility state (see OPCODE.md) |
849: | `EVENT_LISTENERS` | 0x2005 | U32 | Raw pointer listeners (down/move/up) for app-side tap composition |
850: | `COLOR`/`FONT_*`/`PADDING`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/… | — | — | Text & appearance modifiers (MODIFIERS.md) |
851: 
852: - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** no children → native button; the label is the
853:   node's text (`SET_TEXT`). If the text is also absent, render an empty
854:   platform button shell (leaf fallback). Button styles are renderer/token-owned.
855: - **Composite Override Mode (container):** children present → suppress default
856:   button chrome, render the custom label tree, wrap it with a native
857:   click/press gesture that reports `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_UP` for the button's
858:   `ACTION_ID` callback.
859: - **Events:** the tap is the app-side composition of the raw pointer events
860:   (`POINTER_DOWN` then `POINTER_UP` on the same target). Without `ACTION_ID` /
861:   `BINDING_ID` / `EVENT_LISTENERS`, a renderer MUST drop the interaction (Event
862:   Guards).
863: - **Note (SwiftUI `Link`)**: SwiftUI's `Link` is `BUTTON` with an associated
864:   URL; the app handles the tap and opens the URL. No separate primitive.
865: 
866: ### TextField / SecureField — `TEXT_FIELD` 0x21
867: 
868: Single-line text input; `SecureField` is the same component with `IS_SECURE`.
869: 
870: | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
871: |----------|----|------|---------|
872: | `LABEL` | 0x200A | STRING | Caption label |
873: | `PROMPT` | 0x200B | STRING | Placeholder text |
874: | `IS_SECURE` | 0x200D | U8 | 1 = masked input (`SecureField`) |
875: | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (text value) |
876: | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
877: 
878: - **Events** (see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)): `TEXT_CHANGED` (0x07) on every
879:   edit; `FOCUS_CHANGED` (0x08), `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09), `SUBMIT` (0x0A) —
880:   draft. All gated by `BINDING_ID` or the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits.
881: - **Security**: a secure field MUST mask characters and MUST NOT echo the value.
882: 
883: ### TextEditor — `TEXT_EDITOR` 0x22
884: 
885: Multi-line text editing area.
886: 
887: - **Protocol**: a leaf node; content via `SET_TEXT`, value binding via
888:   `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
889: - **Properties**: `LINE_LIMIT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
890:   `IS_SECURE` (unused), text modifiers.
891: - **Events**: same as `TextField` — `TEXT_CHANGED` (0x07), `FOCUS_CHANGED`
892:   (0x08), `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09), `SUBMIT` (0x0A) — gated by `BINDING_ID` /
893:   `EVENT_LISTENERS`.
894: 
895: ### Toggle — `TOGGLE` 0x24
896: 
897: A boolean switch, checkbox, or button control. The **visual style is a token**,
898: not a separate component:
899: 
900: | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
901: |----------|----|------|---------|
902: | `TOGGLE_STYLE` | 0x2018 | F32 (enum) | `Switch`=0 (default), `Checkbox`=1, `Button`=2 |
903: | `SELECTED` | 0x2004 | U8 | Checked state (0 off, 1 on) |
904: | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (bool value) |
905: | `LABEL` | 0x200A | STRING | Optional caption |
906: | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
907: 
908: - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** renders the native control for the
909:   `TOGGLE_STYLE` token — a native switch, checkbox, or toggle button. The style
910:   token switches native variants **without emitting child nodes**.
911: - **Composite Override Mode (container):** a custom body (e.g. label + icon)
912:   wrapped with a native toggle gesture; `SELECTED` still drives the state.
913: - **Events:** a user change emits `VALUE_CHANGED` (0x06) with `B` = 0/1 — gated
914:   by `BINDING_ID`. The app writes it into `SELECTED`; the engine re-emits the
915:   `SELECTED` property.
916: 
917: ### Slider — `SLIDER` 0x25
918: 
919: A continuous or stepped numeric range control.
920: 
921: | Property | ID | Type | Meaning |
922: |----------|----|------|---------|
923: | `VALUE` | 0x2006 | F32 | Current value |
924: | `MIN_VALUE` | 0x2007 | F32 | Inclusive minimum |
925: | `MAX_VALUE` | 0x2008 | F32 | Inclusive maximum |
926: | `STEP_VALUE` | 0x2009 | F32 | Stepped mode increment (default 1.0 if absent; absent = continuous) |
927: | `BINDING_ID` | 0x2017 | U32 | Two-way binding id (numeric value) |
928: | `ENABLED`/`STATE` | 0x2003/0x2002 | — | Enabled / accessibility state |
929: 
930: - **Native Token Mode (leaf):** native slider; the renderer owns 120 FPS
931:   client-side thumb dragging and resolves the semantic value from its own track
932:   geometry.
933: - **Composite Override Mode (container):** a custom track/thumb body wrapped
934:   with a native drag gesture that reports `VALUE_CHANGED`.
935: - **Events:** `VALUE_CHANGED` (0x06, `A=targetId, B=value (f32)`) — gated by
936:   `BINDING_ID`.
937: 
938: ### Stepper — `STEPPER` 0x26
939: 
940: A discrete increment/decrement control. `VALUE` (0x2006), `STEP_VALUE`
941: (0x2009), `MIN_VALUE` (0x2007), `MAX_VALUE` (0x2008), `BINDING_ID` (0x2017).
942: Events: `VALUE_CHANGED` after each press.
943: 
944: ### DatePicker — `DATE_PICKER` 0x27
945: 
946: A date & time selection modal/popover control.

300: /// Assign stable unique sequential ids to a tree (pre-order; root first).
301: ///
302: /// The engine keys its diff snapshot by node id, so call this after building
303: /// the (possibly re-built) tree and before `Engine::emit`.
304: ///
305: /// **Media controllers are pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it
306: /// was first given (spec/MEDIA.md), so a structural swap that shifts other ids
307: /// never changes the playback key — and its `VIDEO` surface's
308: /// `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` is linked in the same pass.
309: pub fn assign_ids(root: &mut Node, next: &mut u32) {
310:     // Reserve every already-pinned controller id up front, so no other node can
311:     // be handed one even when it is lower than the current cursor.
312:     let mut reserved = BTreeSet::new();
313:     collect_pinned_controller_ids(root, &mut reserved);
314:     assign_ids_pass(root, next, &mut reserved);
315: }
316: 
317: /// Collect the ids already pinned by the controllers present in this tree.
318: fn collect_pinned_controller_ids(node: &Node, out: &mut BTreeSet<u32>) {
319:     if matches!(node.component, Component::MediaController) {
320:         if let Some(id) = node
321:             .media_controller
322:             .as_ref()
323:             .map(|c| c.0.pinned_node_id())
324:             .filter(|id| *id != 0)
325:         {
326:             out.insert(id);
327:         }
328:     }
329:     for child in &node.children {
330:         collect_pinned_controller_ids(child, out);
331:     }
332: }
333: 
334: /// Take the next free (unreserved) id from the cursor.
335: fn take_id(next: &mut u32, reserved: &BTreeSet<u32>) -> u32 {
336:     if *next == 0 {
337:         *next = 1;
338:     }
339:     while reserved.contains(next) {
340:         *next += 1;
341:     }
342:     let id = *next;
343:     *next += 1;
344:     id
345: }
346: 
347: fn assign_ids_pass(node: &mut Node, next: &mut u32, reserved: &mut BTreeSet<u32>) {
348:     match (&node.component, node.media_controller.clone()) {
349:         (Component::MediaController, Some(controller)) => {
350:             // A controller keeps the id it was first pinned to.
351:             let pinned = controller.0.pinned_node_id();
352:             node.id = if pinned != 0 {
353:                 pinned
354:             } else {
355:                 let id = take_id(next, reserved);
356:                 controller.0.pin_node_id(id);
357:                 id
358:             };
359:             reserved.insert(node.id);
360:         }
361:         _ => {
362:             node.id = take_id(next, reserved);
363:         }
364:     }
365:     // Link a video surface to its controller (spec/MEDIA.md).
366:     if matches!(node.component, Component::Video) {
367:         if let Some(id) = node
368:             .media_controller
369:             .as_ref()
370:             .map(|c| c.0.pinned_node_id())
371:             .filter(|id| *id != 0)
372:         {
373:             node.properties.insert(property_id::MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID, id);
374:         }
375:     }
376:     for child in &mut node.children {
377:         assign_ids_pass(child, next, reserved);
378:     }
379: }

381: /// Collect a `node id -> tap callback` map from a built (and id-assigned) tree.
382: ///
383: /// Call after [`assign_ids`] so each node has its stable id; the returned map
384: /// keys the recognizer's tap target to the closure registered by
385: /// `.on_tap_gesture(...)`.
386: pub fn collect_tap_handlers(root: &Node, out: &mut BTreeMap<u32, TapHandler>) {
387:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
388:         if let Gesture::Tap(handler) = gesture {
389:             out.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
390:         }
391:     }
392:     for child in &root.children {
393:         collect_tap_handlers(child, out);
394:     }
395: }
396: 
397: /// App-side two-way binding sinks collected from a built (and id-assigned) tree,
398: /// keyed by node id. A host routes the control events into these:
399: /// `TEXT_CHANGED` → [`InputHandlers::text`], `VALUE_CHANGED` →
400: /// [`InputHandlers::value`], `DATE_CHANGED` → [`InputHandlers::date`]. Each sink
401: /// writes its bound signal; re-emit the tree afterwards to flush the delta.
402: #[derive(Default)]
403: pub struct InputHandlers {
404:     /// `TEXT_CHANGED` sinks (text fields / editors).
405:     pub text: BTreeMap<u32, TextInputHandler>,
406:     /// `VALUE_CHANGED` sinks (toggle / slider / stepper / picker / color picker).
407:     pub value: BTreeMap<u32, ValueInputHandler>,
408:     /// `DATE_CHANGED` sinks (date pickers).
409:     pub date: BTreeMap<u32, DateInputHandler>,
410: }
411: 
412: /// Collect the two-way binding sinks from a built (and id-assigned) tree.
413: pub fn collect_input_handlers(root: &Node, out: &mut InputHandlers) {
414:     for gesture in &root.gestures {
415:         match gesture {
416:             Gesture::TextInput(handler) => {
417:                 out.text.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
418:             }
419:             Gesture::ValueInput(handler) => {
420:                 out.value.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
421:             }
422:             Gesture::DateInput(handler) => {
423:                 out.date.insert(root.id, handler.clone());
424:             }
425:             Gesture::Tap(_) => {}
426:         }
427:     }
428:     for child in &root.children {
429:         collect_input_handlers(child, out);
430:     }
431: }

1: //! The app-side media controller state object (spec/MEDIA.md).
2: //!
3: //! A media playback is a **state object**, not a view (the SwiftUI `AVPlayer`
4: //! analog). The controller owns a resource and its transport as
5: //! [signals](crate::signal): the *commands* (`playing`, `position`, `volume`,
6: //! `muted`, `looping`, `rate`) the app/user writes, and the *reports* (`time`,
7: //! `duration`, `volume_report`) the renderer's `MEDIA_*` events feed.
8: //!
9: //! The view DSL materializes **one** non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per
10: //! controller (via `attach()`), so playback identity is stable across structural
11: //! swaps — a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` band change never restarts playback, and any number
12: //! of surfaces/control views referencing the same controller drive the same
13: //! playback. **Audio has no view**: an audio playback is a controller plus
14: //! ordinary views (buttons/sliders) bound to its transport signals.
15:

17: use alloc::string::String;

22: /// A media playback controller.
23: ///
24: /// Build it (creating its signals), rebind the transport slots to the app's own
25: /// signals, then share it (`Rc`) and reference it from surfaces/controls:
26: ///
27: /// ```
28: /// use std::rc::Rc;
29: /// use pathland_engine::{Engine, MediaController};
30: ///
31: /// let engine = Engine::new();
32: /// let rt = engine.runtime();
33: /// let player = Rc::new(
34: ///     MediaController::with_source(&rt, "/assets/track1.mp3")
35: ///         .on_ended(|| { /* next track */ }),
36: /// );
37: /// player.play();
38: /// ```
39: pub struct MediaController {
40:     /// The reactive runtime the signals live on.
41:     runtime: Runtime,
42:     /// The resource: a static URL/asset, or a reactive binding (current track).
43:     source: Signal<String>,
44:     /// Play/pause command (`PLAYBACK_STATE`).
45:     playing: WritableSignal<bool>,
46:     /// Seek command (`MEDIA_POSITION`, seconds).
47:     position: WritableSignal<f32>,
48:     /// Volume command (`MEDIA_VOLUME`, 0..1).
49:     volume: WritableSignal<f32>,
50:     /// Mute command (`MEDIA_MUTED`), independent of `volume`.
51:     muted: WritableSignal<bool>,
52:     /// Loop-on-end command (`MEDIA_LOOP`).
53:     looping: WritableSignal<bool>,
54:     /// Playback rate command (`MEDIA_RATE`, 1.0 = normal).
55:     rate: WritableSignal<f32>,
56:     /// Position report feed (`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`).
57:     time: WritableSignal<f32>,
58:     /// Duration report feed (`MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`) — a seek control's max.
59:     duration: WritableSignal<f32>,
60:     /// Volume report feed (`MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED`) — bind a display to it.
61:     volume_report: WritableSignal<f32>,
62:     /// The end-of-media hook (`MEDIA_ENDED`).
63:     on_ended: RefCell<Option<Rc<dyn Fn()>>>,
64:     /// The node id this controller's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node is pinned to
65:     /// (`0` until the first [`assign_ids`](crate::assign_ids) pass).
66:     node_id: Cell<u32>,
67: }

1: # pathland-engine — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 9, 2026
4: 
5: The retained-tree **emitter**: the application's canonical UI tree and the
6: diff-based reactive emission into `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes. Protocol contract:
7: `spec/`.
8: 
9: ## Implemented
10: 
11: - **Retained tree** (`node.rs`): `Node` (id, component, children, properties,
12:   `string_properties`, `token_properties`, text/property signal bindings,
13:   app-side gestures). Components include `Icon` (→ `component_type::ICON`).
14: - **String-valued properties**: `Node::string_properties` (property → value,
15:   e.g. `FONT_FAMILY`, `LABEL`, `IMAGE_SOURCE`) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the
16:   `STRING` value type (arena-allocated); unchanged strings reuse their arena
17:   offset — steady-state emission stays zero-alloc with string props present
18:   (proven by test).
19: - **Components** (`Component` enum): the full spec set — `VStack`, `HStack`,
20:   `ZStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape`, `Divider`,
21:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`,
22:   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`,
23:   `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` — all mapped to
24:   `component_type` ids via `component_type_id`.
25: - **Diff emitter** (`engine.rs`): create/delete/insert/move deltas,
26:   property/text deltas, steady-state zero emission.
27: - **Design-token property refs**: `Node::token_properties` (property → token
28:   path) emit as `SET_PROPERTY` with the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type; unchanged
29:   refs reuse their arena offset across passes — **steady-state emission stays
30:   zero-alloc with token refs present** (proven by test).
31: - **`Engine::set_design_token`** — emits a global `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
32:   override (base or `dark.`-prefixed) into the current frame.
33: - **Global theme overrides** (`theme.rs`): `Theme` — single-value builders
34:   (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme { light,
35:   dark }` composes a light + dark pair. `Engine::apply_theme` (light-only) and
36:   `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light as base, dark with the `dark.` prefix;
37:   STRING values arena-alloc'd) emit the overrides once at mount — they never
38:   re-emit nodes.
39: - **Reactive runtime** (`signal.rs`): a shared `Runtime`
40:   (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; the "current computation"
41:   is an explicit stack in the store) owns value signals, **computed** signals
42:   (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and **effects** (run
43:   immediately, then on dependency change) plus `untracked` reads. Typed handles
44:   `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (`SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`);
45:   `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. Node text/properties bound
46:   to a signal re-emit only the bound node on change — including a computed's
47:   bound nodes (`set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps).
48: - **Signals bound to node text/properties**: `set_signal` re-emits only the
49:   bound nodes (`SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`); `get_signal` returns the current value.
50: - **Gestures / input sinks**: `Gesture::Tap` (app-side callback) plus the
51:   two-way binding sinks `Gesture::ValueInput`/`TextInput`/`DateInput` (with
52:   `TapHandler`/`ValueInputHandler`/`TextInputHandler`/`DateInputHandler` aliases).
53:   `collect_tap_handlers` and `collect_input_handlers` (→ `InputHandlers`) expose
54:   the app-side registries; sinks are never serialized.
55: - **Media controller** (`media.rs`, spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the
56:   app-side state object owning a resource (`source`/`bind_source`) and its
57:   transport as signals: commands `playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/
58:   `looping`/`rate` (each rebindable to an app-owned signal), report feeds
59:   `time`/`duration`/`volume_report`, `on_ended`, and the convenience transport
60:   (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`set_volume`/`set_muted`/`set_looping`/
61:   `set_rate`). A node references one through the identity-compared
62:   `MediaControllerRef` (`Node.media_controller`); `Component::MediaController`
63:   (0x30, non-visual) is the controller's node and `Component::Video` is its
64:   surface. **Audio has no view.**
65: - **String property bindings** (`Node.string_bindings`): a `STRING`-valued
66:   property bound to a signal (e.g. a controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) re-emits only
67:   that property (`SET_PROPERTY`, `STRING`, arena-allocated) on change — a track
68:   change emits exactly one opcode.
69: - **`assign_ids`** (pre-order stable ids) — and **media controllers are
70:   pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it was first given, so a
71:   structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the playback key; the same
72:   pass links each `VIDEO` surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` to the controller node.
73: 
74: ## Not implemented / gaps
75: 
76: - Only the `Tap` gesture plus value/text/date input sinks; no other gesture.
77: - Signal-bound properties cannot carry token refs (a token ref is a static path).
78: - `get_signal` returns an owned value (the store is shared via `Rc<RefCell>`).
79: 
80: ## Verified by
81: 
82: `cargo test -p pathland-engine` — emitter deltas, signals (values, computed,
83: effects, `untracked`), `component_type_id`.

1: //! Diff-based reactive emitter.
2: //!
3: //! The engine holds the application's retained view tree and emits the
4: //! declarative structure as `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
5: //! buffer (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment). It does not
6: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers lay out their own elements.
7: //!
8: //! Emission is diff-based: on each `emit` the engine compares the current tree
9: //! against a snapshot of what it last emitted and writes only the opcodes for
10: //! nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
11: //!
12: //! The emit pass performs zero dynamic heap allocations in the steady state.
13: //!
14: //! ## Signals
15: //!
16: //! Nodes may bind their text or a property to a [`crate::SignalId`]. The engine
17: //! resolves those bindings during emit (recording the dependency) and re-emits
18: //! only the affected nodes on [`Engine::set_signal`] — no full tree walk.
19: 
20: use alloc::borrow::ToOwned;
21: use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;
22: use alloc::string::{String, ToString};
23: use alloc::vec;
24: use alloc::vec::Vec;
25: 
26: use pathland_core::{value_type, value_type_for};
27: use pathland_core::Guest;
28: 
29: use crate::node::{component_type_id, Component, Node};
30: use crate::signal::{Dep, Runtime, Signal, SignalId, SignalValue, SignalValueKind, WritableSignal};

32: /// Encode a `LIST` property's arena entry: `[u32 count][f32 × count]`
33: /// (spec/OPCODE.md §Value types — a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
34: fn encode_list(values: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
35:     let mut bytes = vec![0u8; 4 + 4 * values.len()];
36:     bytes[0..4].copy_from_slice(&(values.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
37:     for (i, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
38:         let o = 4 + 4 * i;
39:         bytes[o..o + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
40:     }
41:     bytes
42: }
43: 
44: /// Per-node state the engine remembers from the last emission.
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
46: struct SnapshotNode {
47:     component_type: u16,
48:     parent: Option<u32>,
49:     index: usize,
50:     text: Option<String>,
51:     properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
52:     /// Last-emitted `STRING` properties: property → (value, arena offset). The
53:     /// arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged string never
54:     /// re-allocates into the bump arena.
55:     string_properties: BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>,
56:     /// Last-emitted `LIST` properties: property → (values, arena offset). The
57:     /// arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged list never
58:     /// re-allocates into the bump arena.
59:     list_properties: BTreeMap<u16, (Vec<f32>, u32)>,
60:     /// Last-emitted `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs: property → (token path, arena offset).
61:     /// The arena offset is reused across passes so an unchanged ref never
62:     /// re-allocates into the bump arena.
63:     token_refs: BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>,
64:     /// Generation stamp set on each emit pass; used to detect deleted nodes.
65:     gen: u64,
66: }

72:     pub opcodes: usize,
73: }

75: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
76: ///
77: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted and owns the signal
78: /// store. Calling `emit` with a (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only
79: /// the delta opcodes; `set_signal` writes deltas for only the bound nodes.
80: pub struct Engine {
81:     /// nodeId to last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
82:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
83:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
84:     gen: u64,
85:     /// Reactive signal runtime (values + computed/effects + node dependencies).
86:     store: Runtime,
87: }
88: 
89: impl Default for Engine {
90:     fn default() -> Self {
91:         Self::new()
92:     }
93: }
94: 
95: impl Engine {
96:     pub fn new() -> Self {
97:         Self {
98:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
99:             gen: 0,
100:             store: Runtime::new(),
101:         }
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// The shared reactive runtime (for creating typed signals / computeds).
105:     pub fn runtime(&self) -> Runtime {
106:         self.store.clone()
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
110:     pub fn emit(
111:         &mut self,
112:         root: &Node,
113:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
114:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_core::RingError> {
115:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
116:         // Rebuild the signal->node dependency index from scratch; reconcile
117:         // re-adds the bindings this tree actually uses, so stale subscriptions
118:         // vanish.
119:         self.store.clear_node_deps();
120:         let mut out = 0usize;
121:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
122: 
123:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
124:             if let Some(s) = slot {
125:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
126:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
127:                     out += 1;
128:                     *slot = None;
129:                 }
130:             }
131:         }
132:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
133:     }
134: 
135:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
136:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {
137:         self.snapshot.iter().filter(|s| s.is_some()).count()
138:     }

140:     /// Emit a global design-token override (`PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`).
141:     /// Overrides are renderer-global and apply everywhere the renderer resolves
142:     /// tokens; a `dark.`-prefixed path overrides the dark variant
143:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md). Returns the arena offset of the token path.
144:     pub fn set_design_token(
145:         &mut self,
146:         path: &str,
147:         value_type: u8,
148:         value: u32,
149:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
150:     ) -> Result<u32, pathland_core::RingError> {
151:         guest.set_design_token(path, value_type, value)
152:     }
153: 
154:     /// Emit a batch of global design-token overrides ([`Theme`](crate::Theme))
155:     /// as `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes. `STRING`-valued overrides allocate
156:     /// their value into the guest arena first (the wire carries an arena ref).
157:     ///
158:     /// Overrides are renderer-global: they never re-emit nodes and are not part
159:     /// of the diff. Emit once at mount, before the tree.
160:     pub fn apply_theme(
161:         &mut self,
162:         theme: &crate::Theme,
163:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
164:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
165:         for (path, value) in theme.iter() {
166:             self.emit_token_override(path, value, guest)?;
167:         }
168:         Ok(())
169:     }
170: 
171:     /// Emit an adaptive theme ([`AdaptiveTheme`](crate::AdaptiveTheme)): the
172:     /// **light** theme's overrides as base tokens, the **dark** theme's with the
173:     /// `dark.` scheme prefix (spec/TOKENS.md).
174:     pub fn apply_adaptive_theme(
175:         &mut self,
176:         adaptive: &crate::AdaptiveTheme,
177:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
178:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
179:         self.apply_theme(&adaptive.light, guest)?;
180:         for (path, value) in adaptive.dark.iter() {
181:             let dark_path = if path.starts_with("dark.") {
182:                 path.to_string()
183:             } else {
184:                 alloc::format!("dark.{path}")
185:             };
186:             self.emit_token_override(&dark_path, value, guest)?;
187:         }
188:         Ok(())
189:     }
190: 
191:     /// Emit one `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override, arena-allocating STRING values.
192:     fn emit_token_override(
193:         &mut self,
194:         path: &str,
195:         value: &pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue,
196:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
197:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
198:         use pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue;
199:         match value {
200:             TokenValue::Str(s) => {
201:                 let ref_ = guest
202:                     .alloc_str(s)
203:                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
204:                 guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), ref_)?;
205:             }
206:             _ => {
207:                 if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
208:                     guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), bits)?;
209:                 }
210:             }
211:         }
212:         Ok(())
213:     }
