242:     /// Write a typed writable signal and re-emit only the nodes bound to it.
243:     pub fn set<T: SignalValueKind>(
244:         &mut self,
245:         signal: WritableSignal<T>,
246:         value: T,
247:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
248:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {

255:     }

257:     /// Replace a signal's value and re-emit only the nodes that depend on it
258:     /// (including nodes bound to any computed signal it feeds).
259:     ///
260:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas for the bound nodes whose
261:     /// materialized value changed. Returns the number of opcodes written.
262:     pub fn set_signal(
263:         &mut self,
264:         id: SignalId,
265:         value: SignalValue,
266:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
267:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
268:         let changed = self.store.set(id, value);
269:         let mut out = 0usize;
270:         for cell in changed {
271:             out += self.emit_cell(cell, guest)?;
272:         }
273:         Ok(out)
274:     }

276:     /// Re-emit the node bindings on one (changed) signal.
277:     fn emit_cell(
278:         &mut self,
279:         id: SignalId,
280:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
281:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
282:         let deps: Vec<Dep> = self.store.node_deps(id);
283:         if deps.is_empty() {
284:             return Ok(0);
285:         }
286:         let value = self.store.get(id);
287:         let mut out = 0usize;
288:         for dep in deps {
289:             match dep {
290:                 Dep::Text { node } => {
291:                     let new_text: Option<String> = value.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned);
292:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_text(node);
293:                     if new_text.as_deref() != prev_text {
294:                         if let Some(t) = new_text.as_deref() {
295:                             guest.set_text(node, t)?;
296:                             out += 1;
297:                         }
298:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
299:                             s.text = new_text;
300:                         }
301:                     }
302:                 }
303:                 Dep::Property { node, prop } => {
304:                     let new_value = value.to_property_u32();
305:                     let prev_value = self.snapshot_property(node, prop);
306:                     if new_value != prev_value {
307:                         if let Some(v) = new_value {
308:                             guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type_for(prop), v)?;
309:                             out += 1;
310:                         }
311:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
312:                             match new_value {
313:                                 Some(v) => {
314:                                     s.properties.insert(prop, v);
315:                                 }
316:                                 None => {
317:                                     s.properties.remove(&prop);
318:                                 }
319:                             }
320:                         }
321:                     }
322:                 }
323:                 Dep::StringProperty { node, prop } => {
324:                     let new_text: Option<String> = value.to_text().map(ToOwned::to_owned);
325:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_string(node, prop).map(ToOwned::to_owned);
326:                     if new_text != prev_text {
327:                         let emitted = match new_text.as_deref() {
328:                             Some(t) => {
329:                                 let arena = guest
330:                                     .alloc_str(t)
331:                                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
332:                                 guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type::STRING, arena)?;
333:                                 out += 1;
334:                                 Some((t.to_string(), arena))
335:                             }
336:                             None => None,
337:                         };
338:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
339:                             match emitted {
340:                                 Some((v, arena)) => {
341:                                     s.string_properties.insert(prop, (v, arena));
342:                                 }
343:                                 None => {
344:                                     s.string_properties.remove(&prop);
345:                                 }
346:                             }

324:         return new View() {
325:             @Override
326:             public PathlandNode render(Environment env) {
327:                 View nested = SizeThatFits.make(Fit.of(Text.make(t -> t.text("wide")), 600f),

334:     private static int slotByThreshold(RenderResult result, ProtocolFrame frame, float threshold) {
335:         for (int id : result.fitInputs().keySet()) {
336:             Opcode query = frame.opcodes().stream()
337:                     .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER
338:                             && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
339:                             && o.a() == id && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.FIT_QUERY)
340:                     .findFirst().orElseThrow();
341:             byte[] strings = frame.strings();
342:             int offset = query.c();
343:             int count = le32(strings, offset);
344:             for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
345:                 if (Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 4 + i * 4)) == threshold) {
346:                     return id;
347:                 }
348:             }
349:         }
350:         throw new AssertionError("no slot with threshold " + threshold);
351:     }
352: 
353:     private static int slotId(RenderResult result) {
354:         return result.fitInputs().keySet().iterator().next();
355:     }
356: 
357:     private static long count(ProtocolFrame frame, int command) {
358:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
359:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == command)
360:                 .count();
361:     }
362: 
363:     private static long countOps(ProtocolFrame frame, int category, int command) {
364:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
365:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == category && o.command() == command)
366:                 .count();
367:     }
368: 
369:     private static boolean containsText(ProtocolFrame frame, String text) {
370:         return frame.opcodes().stream()
371:                 .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT)
372:                 .anyMatch(o -> frame.stringAt(o.b()).contains(text));
373:     }

431:     private static int le32(byte[] bytes, int offset) {
432:         return (bytes[offset] & 0xFF)

438:     /** The `FIT_QUERY` threshold table (LIST value in the arena) for a fit slot. */
439:     private static float[] fitThresholds(ProtocolFrame frame, int slotId) {
440:         for (Opcode op : frame.opcodes()) {
441:             if (op.category() == Categories.PARAMETER && op.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
442:                     && op.a() == slotId && (op.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.FIT_QUERY) {
443:                 byte[] strings = frame.strings();
444:                 int offset = op.c();
445:                 int count = le32(strings, offset);
446:                 float[] thresholds = new float[count];
447:                 for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
448:                     thresholds[i] = Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 4 + i * 4));
449:                 }
450:                 return thresholds;
451:             }
452:         }
453:         throw new AssertionError("no FIT_QUERY for slot " + slotId);
454:     }

457:      *  root MusicPlayerView row at 1024f, the player-bar controls group at 700f). */

459:         for (Opcode op : frame.opcodes()) {
460:             if (op.category() == Categories.TREE && op.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE
461:                     && op.b() == Components.SIZE_THAT_FITS) {
462:                 float[] thresholds = fitThresholds(frame, op.a());
463:                 if (thresholds[thresholds.length - 1] == maxThreshold) {
464:                     return op.a();
465:                 }
466:             }
467:         }
468:         throw new AssertionError("no fit slot with max threshold " + maxThreshold);

1: # pathland-view (Java) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 15, 2026
4: 
5: The hand-written, framework-agnostic Java 17+ DSL (`dev.pathland.view`):
6: declarative views, Angular-style signals, fine-grained emitter, `PLPL` wire
7: codec, lazy JNA ring interop, and cross-platform `State`. Protocol contract:
8: `spec/`. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
9: 
10: ## Implemented
11: 
12: - **`ProxyView`** (`ProxyView.make(p -> p.endpoint(...).route(...).credential(...))`):
13:   a `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) container whose child subtree is served by **another**
14:   Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md). It authors **no** children — the origin root is
15:   spliced in at runtime — and takes size modifiers like any view. The immutable
16:   `ProxyConfig` snapshot rides the node (`PathlandNode.proxyConfig`) and is
17:   surfaced to the host through `RenderResult.proxyViews()` (node id → config) so
18:   `pathland-server-core` opens an origin connection per proxy node. The emitter's
19:   internal `onStructureReconciled(Runnable)` hook (like `snapshotEmission`) fires
20:   after each structural reconcile — after the routing maps reflect the new subtree
21:   — so the host reconciles origin connections against the live `proxyViews` map
22:   (a proxy lives exactly while its node is in the retained tree, spec/PROXY.md §7).
23: - **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
24:   a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
25:   thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
26:   The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
27:   (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
28:   the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
29:   value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
30:   (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
31:   state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
32:   slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
33:   with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
34:   the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
35:   controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
36:   compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
37:   unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
38:   internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
39:   `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
40:   order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
41:   correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
42:   gates the mount-time structural effect so the multi-candidate presentation is
43:   not collapsed before the renderer reports; the first `FIT_CHANGED` (recorded
44:   before the incoming index) downgrades the slot to the single selected child via
45:   the normal reconcile, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The
46:   downgrade is a **clean N→1**: it keeps the SELECTED candidate's node as-is
47:   (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it never
48:   positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same component
49:   and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner into
50:   the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
51: - **v2 authoring surface (complete)**: every concrete view exposes
52:   the three operations — values via the static `View.make(...)`
53:   (`make(Consumer<Config>)`, `make(value)` shortcuts, empty `make()`),
54:   `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` (an **instance** operation — the `View` interface
55:   ships a `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` so a bare `View` value
56:   (a style's `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) applies modifiers too, and
57:   `ViewBuilder` overrides it covariantly), and (content-bearing views) `.children(View...)`
58:   (static first-call retained as a value-less convenience). Values are configured
59:   via `make(c -> …)`, the chain lives on the returned generic
60:   `ViewBuilder<V, C>` (`View.Config`, `Configurable<C>`, `ChildrenView`; `View`
61:   keeps only `body()`/`render()`/`modifiers(...)` — Java's static-vs-instance rule
62:   means `make(...)` is the only static of the three; the former static
63:   `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points are **removed**). Modifiers/styles are
64:   built through the **`Modifiers` facade's lowercase functions** — one
65:   `import static dev.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` brings the whole vocabulary
66:   (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `frame(f -> f.width(100).height(24))`,
67:   `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`, `borderedButtonStyle(b -> …)`); the
68:   former per-type `with(...)` configurators are **removed** (a same-package
69:   construction seam remains for the facade). **Single-value modifiers are the value
70:   itself** (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`,
71:   `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.LARGE`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`,
72:   `FontDesign.SERIF`, `Font.system(18)` — the enums + `Font` implement
73:   `ViewModifier`), and `Style extends ViewModifier`, so `.modifiers(MyButtonStyle)`
74:   scopes the matching environment key — an app-authored style exposes a lowercase
75:   static factory on its own type (`BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(s -> s…)`).
76:   The `View` per-modifier sugar
77:   (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange`), the former
78:   `View.with(ViewModifier...)` general modifier chain, and the `*Mod` shims
79:   (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
80:   `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed** —
81:   every consumer (demo views, starters, renderers) is on the v3 surface. The
82:   former `.of(...)` **construction factories are removed**: a **single-value
83:   construction overload** replaces them where the config has
84:   a designated primary member (views `make(value)` — `Text.make("hi")`;
85:   modifiers the lowercase value form — `padding(16)`,
86:   `fontSize(sizeSignal)` — pure sugar for the lambda, via the package-private
87:   `Configurators` helper), and the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty `make()` (for
88:   config-less or value-less views) covers the rest. Only data/branch factories keep
89:   `of` (`Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`,
90:   `Params.of`). The `View` interface carries no per-modifier factory
91:   methods (spec `DSL.md` §5.6).
92: - **Signals-first configs (spec DSL.md §2)**: **every value member** exposes a raw
93:   setter (sugar for `Signals.constant`) and a `Signal<T>` setter — layout included
94:   (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`/`tracks`, …). A
95:   non-constant signal becomes a **node-level binding** (re-emits only that
96:   property); a constant carries zero binding overhead. Two-way control *values*
97:   take `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`
98:   (`WritableSignal extends Signal`). Views and modifiers place values through the
99:   single `PathlandNode.property(id, Signal<?>)` path; `emit.ReactiveValues`
100:   coerces a signal's value to the property's declared wire type
101:   (`ValueTypes.forProperty`) and maps `WireValue` enums to their numeric code.
102:   `State`/`Signals` are unchanged.
103: - **Construction**: every concrete view/control is
104:   built with <View>.make(c -> …) / .children(...) / .modifiers(...)
105:   (`Text.make(t -> t.text("x"))` or the shortcut `Text.make("x")`,
106:   `VStack.make(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(a, b)`,
107:   `Button.make(b -> b.action(...)).children(label)`,
108:   `Slider.make(s -> s.value(binding).in(min, max))`,
109:   `DatePicker.make(d -> d.selection(days))`, …). `Slider`/`Stepper` are
110:   binding-first (initial value read from the signal). Grids take
111:   their track counts as config values: `Grid.make(g -> g.columns(int[, rows]), …)`,
112:   `LazyVGrid.make(g -> g.columns(int), …)`, `LazyHGrid.make(g -> g.rows(int), …)` — absent = auto-fit
113:   (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §grid model); the counts emit `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`,
114:   never a pixel `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`. **Per-track sizes** via a `List<GridItem>`
115:   overload (`GridItem.flexible()` / `.fixed(pts)` / `.adaptive(min)`) emit the
116:   `GRID_TRACKS` STRING spec (takes precedence over the counts); CSS-grid-native —
117: - **Alignment is three typed enums, all position-only**:
118:   `HorizontalAlignment` (leading/center/trailing) for `VStack`s,
119:   `VerticalAlignment` (top/center/bottom) for `HStack`s, and a 2D `Alignment`
120:   (topLeading…bottomTrailing) for `ZStack`s, grids, and the `Frame` modifier's content
121:   placement — all encoding the single wire `ALIGNMENT` 2D code (0–8, spec
122:   PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). Stretching is a child's `FILL` size kind, never an
123:   alignment.
124:   GTK falls back to natural sizing (see render-gtk status).
125: - **One modifier mechanism — no sugar on `View`**: core modifiers are
126:   `ViewModifier` values built via `padding(c -> …)` (`Modifiers.*` lowercase function)
127:   (`padding(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(c))`,
128:   `border(b -> b.color(c).width(w))`, …) or passed as the bare value when the
129:   value *is* the modifier (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, `MyButtonStyle`),
130:   applied via `.modifiers(...)` (one or several,
131:   innermost-first); sizing is the `Frame` modifier value — the lambda
132:   configurator `frame(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` /
133:   `frame(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))` (the fluent
134:   `Frame.Config`: min/ideal/max bounds + optional fixed axes + alignment, all
135:   freely combinable). The width/height setters leave `ALIGNMENT` unset
136:   (alignment optional, so a stack's own cross-axis alignment is preserved);
137:   `±∞` width/height is normalized to `Commands.Size.FILL` and `NaN` omits the
138:   axis; an infinite min/ideal/max bound is omitted (no limit).
139:   The `View` interface has **no per-modifier factory methods** (application
140:   authors' views share the modifier-value surface — spec `DSL.md` §5.6), and
141:   the `*Mod` shims are removed. A style is itself a modifier: `buttonStyle` is a
142:   `ButtonStyle` value (an **environment** binding — it scopes
143:   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE`, an `EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`, down the subtree).
144:   `labelStyle` is a `LabelStyle` value (it scopes `Environment.LABEL_STYLE`, an
145:   `EnvironmentKey<LabelStyle>`; `LabelStyle` is an **interface** with
146:   `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnlyLabelStyle`/`IconOnlyLabelStyle`; the style shapes
147:   the emitted child tree, never a wire property).
148: - **One styleable-control contract (spec `DSL.md` §5.7)**: a `Style` supplies a
149:   control's **content** via `makeBody(Configuration)`; the control owns its native
150:   component + interaction and attaches the content as its child (Composite Override
151:   Mode). `Button` renders a `BUTTON` node and wires the action/`EVENT_LISTENERS` on
152:   it (whole button tappable); `ButtonStyle.Configuration` carries only the label, so
153:   a style decorates content and never installs the tap. `PlainButtonStyle` returns
154:   the label, `BorderedButtonStyle` decorates it. `Video` renders a `VIDEO` node
155:   and attaches the active style's control UI as its child (the `EmptyContent`
156:   sentinel = native controls, no child). Label parts are passed to
157:   `LabelStyle` (nullable; `hasTitle()`/`hasIcon()`).
158:   Reactive values
159:   (`foregroundStyle(f -> f.color(signal))`, `background(b -> b.color(signal))`,
160:   `fontSize(s -> s.size(signal))`)
161:   re-emit only the bound node. Value-is-modifier enum types carry **no `Mod`
162:   suffix** (`FontWeight`, `TextAlignment`, `Truncation`, `TextCase`,
163:   `FontStyle`, `FontDesign`, `ControlSize`); the `frame` sizing type is
164:   `Frame`; the wire batch type is `emit.ProtocolFrame` (renamed from `emit.Frame`,
165:   so the modifier name is unambiguous).
166: - **Views**: `View` (open interface), `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Group`
167:   (transparent container, maps to a `VSTACK` node today), `Text`, `Image`,
168:   `Video`,
169:   `Color` (dual identity: a `COLOR` view *and* a value passed into style
170:   modifiers), shapes (`Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Capsule`, `Ellipse`,
171:   `RoundedRectangle`, generic `Shape.make(ShapeKind)` — all `SHAPE` nodes),
172:   `Button`, `TextField`, `Spacer`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
173:   `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Divider`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVStack`,
174:   `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker`,
175:   `DatePicker`, **`Label`** (a composite — an `HStack` of an optional `Image` and
176:   an optional `Text`, title always driving the accessibility label; static and
177:   reactive `Signal<String>` title/icon overloads; the scoped `LabelStyle` decides
178:   which parts render); `body()` composition; `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`ViewModifier`/`Environment`
179:   (the environment is the **only** inheritance mechanism, Java 17+ — a
180:   hierarchical `EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` scope over the synchronous
181:   render pass; no modifier scopes values by any other route).
182: - **Media** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` — the non-visual app-side state
183:   object owning the resource and transport as signals. It exposes the *command*
184:   signals (`source`/`playing`/`position`/`volume`/`muted`/`loop`/`rate`, each
185:   rebindable to an app-owned `WritableSignal` so the controller drives the state
186:   the rest of the UI reads), the *report* feeds
187:   (`time`/`duration`/`volumeReport`), `onEnded`, and the convenience transport
188:   (`play`/`pause`/`toggle`/`seek`/`setVolume`/`setMuted`/`setLoop`/`setRate`).
189:   The emitter materializes **one `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node per controller** (in
190:   place at its `attach()` marker, with a **pinned** id). The pinned id is
191:   reserved in the id allocator (no other node can take it) and honored on **every**
192:   emission path — including a subtree re-emission that reassigns ids (`freshIdFor`)
193:   — so the playback key survives a content swap / band swap and the renderer never
194:   tears down playback. A controller must therefore be created **once** by the app
195:   (a view field, not inline in a route/destination factory: `body()` re-runs on a
196:   path change and would make a new controller); `Video` is the only media view (a `VIDEO`
197:   surface referencing the controller), and **audio has no view** — the app binds
198:   its own buttons/sliders. `VideoStyle` supplies a custom control surface; the
199:   default (`EmptyContent`) keeps the node a leaf with renderer-native controls.
200:   A **`MediaInput`** + `RenderResult.mediaInputs` route the `MEDIA_*` events
201:   (spec/EVENTS.md; `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`) into the bound signals via
202:   `InputDispatcher`; the report feeds are separate from the command binding, so a
203:   report never echoes back as a seek/volume command (spec/EVENTS.md Media echo
204:   guard). `Commands.Event`/`transport.Event`/`FrameCodec` decode the events.
205: - **Component IDs**: synced to the spec's grouped ranges (`Components.java`:
206:   `TEXT 0x01`, `IMAGE 0x02`, `COLOR 0x03`, `SHAPE 0x04`, `DIVIDER 0x05`,
207:   `SPACER 0x06`, `PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07`, `GAUGE 0x08`, `VSTACK 0x10`,
208:   `HSTACK 0x11`, `ZSTACK 0x12`, `GRID 0x13`, `SCROLLVIEW 0x14`, `LAZY_*`,
209:   `BUTTON 0x20`, `TEXT_FIELD 0x21`, `TEXT_EDITOR 0x22`, `TOGGLE 0x24`,
210:   `SLIDER 0x25`, `STEPPER 0x26`, `DATE_PICKER 0x27`, `PICKER 0x28`,
211:   `MENU 0x29`, `COLOR_PICKER 0x2A`, `COMMENT 0x7F`, …) — frames are spec-valid
212:   and cross-language correct.
213: - **Value controls**: `Toggle`/`Slider`/`Stepper`/`Picker`/`ColorPicker`/
214:   `Menu` bind to writable signals and route `VALUE_CHANGED` through the
215:   emitter's value-input registry; `TextEditor` mirrors `TextField`.
216:   `DatePicker` emits `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` (and re-emits it on signal change via a
217:   node-level date binding) and routes `DATE_CHANGED` through a dedicated
218:   date-input registry (`RenderResult.dateInputs`).
219:   `Slider.make(s -> s.value(binding).in(min, max).onEditingChanged(..))` sets the
220:   **`EDITING`** listener bit and routes
221:   **`EDITING_CHANGED`** drag boundaries into the callback through a dedicated
222:   editing-input registry (`RenderResult.editingInputs`, `InputDispatcher`) — the
223:   spec/EVENTS.md `onEditingChanged` hook for seek-on-release etc.
224: - **Events**: the full catalog round-trips — pointer, `KEY_*`, `VALUE_CHANGED`,
225:   `TEXT_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`, `EDITING_CHANGED`, `SUBMIT`, `SCROLL`,
226:   `WHEEL`, `DATE_CHANGED`; listener bits `0..9` declared
227:   (`Commands.Listeners`). `FrameCodec.decodeEvents` decodes all of them.
228: - **Resync**: `Commands.Meta.RESYNC`, `FrameCodec.encodeResync`/`isResync`
229:   (host → guest `META::RESYNC` request), and `Emitter.renderFull()` (re-emit the
230:   complete retained tree as one snapshot frame — no re-mount).
231: - **Heartbeat**: `Commands.Meta.PING`/`PONG` + `FrameCodec.isPing`/`encodePing`/`encodePong`/`encodeEnvironment`
232:   (spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat — **network batch transport only**, never
233:   routed into the app): the server answers a client `META::PING` with a
234:   `META::PONG` batch so the DOM client can detect a silently-stalled connection.
235: - **Message sequence**: `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)` stamps the
236:   batch header's per-stream **message sequence** (`FrameCodec.sequence(bytes)`
237:   reads it); `META::RESYNC`/`PING`/`PONG`/`ENVIRONMENT`/event batches carry `0`.
238:   Consumers detect a lost batch by a sequence gap and recover with a snapshot
239:   (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection).

241:   chainable on any view): `Padding`, `ForegroundStyle(Color)` (no `.color()`),
242:   `Background(Color)`, `Tint`, `Opacity`, `FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `Border`
243:   (`border(b -> b.color(color).width(w))` canonical + `radius`),
244:   `Visible`/`Hidden`, `frame` (`Frame` — the `frame(f -> …)`
245:   configurator: `width`/`height`/`alignment` + min/ideal/max bounds; the former
246:   `Frame.of*`/`ofWidth`/`ofHeight` factories are removed), `Offset`, `Position`,
247:   `FixedSize`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `AspectRatio`/`ScaledToFit`/
248:   `ScaledToFill`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `FontStyle`/`Italic`/`FontDesign`/
249:   `FontWidth`/`Kerning`/`Tracking`/`BaselineOffset`/`LineSpacing`/`LineLimit`/
250:   `TextAlignment`/`Truncation`/`TextCase`/`Underline`/`Strikethrough`/
251:   `FontFamily`, `CornerRadius`, `Shadow`, `Blur`, `Saturation`/`Contrast`/
252:   `Brightness`/`Grayscale`/`HueRotation`/`ColorMultiply`/`ColorInvert`,
253:   `Clipped`/`ClipShape`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect`, `Disabled`,
254:   `AllowsHitTesting`, `ControlSize`,
255:   `AccessibilityLabel`/`AccessibilityRole`/`AccessibilityState`, `ImageSource`,
256:   `PointerEvents` (OR-in), `ActionId`/`BindingId`, `TapGesture` (onTapGesture),
257:   `ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `VideoStyle`,
258:   `EnvironmentBinding`, `PathChange`, `NavigationIntent` — `Color` is never a
259:   modifier.
260:   `AccessibilityLabel`/`Image` accept reactive `Signal<String>` overloads
261:   (node-level `LABEL`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` bindings).
262: - **`Roles` constants** (`dev.pathland.view.Roles`): the canonical **semantic**
263:   `ROLE` catalog (mirrors `pathland_core::constants::role` / `spec/OPCODE.md`,
264:   dense 0–13): `HEADER`, `PARAGRAPH`, `LIST`, `LIST_ITEM`, `SUMMARY`, `BANNER`,
265:   `NAVIGATION`, `MAIN`, `CONTENT_INFO`, `COMPLEMENTARY`, `ARTICLE`, `SECTION`,
266:   `SEARCH`. Interactive/control roles are NOT roles — they are intrinsic to the
267:   control components, so `accessibilityRole(int)` **throws** for codes
268:   outside the semantic catalog (a custom button uses `Button` + `ButtonStyle`).
269: - **`Icon` + `IconName`** (the `ICON` primitive, spec/ICONS.md): a canonical
270:   `IconName` written once and mapped by each renderer to its native symbol
271:   (Adwaita on GTK, Lucide on the web). `Icon.make(i -> i.name(IconName))` /
272:   `Icon.make(i -> i.name(String))` / `Icon.make(i -> i.name(Signal<String>))` /
273:   `Icon.labeled(…, label)`;
274:   `Label.make(l -> l.title(..).icon(View))` composes the icon part;
275:   a reactive name re-emits only `ICON_NAME`. Size/tint follow `FONT_SIZE` /
276:   `COLOR`; `LABEL` makes the icon presentable.
277: - **`Font` (is itself the modifier)** — the `Font` spec: a
278:   predefined typography (`Font.title2()` → `TEXT_STYLE`, heading styles imply a
279:   heading element), a custom family + size (`Font.custom(name, size)` →
280:   `FONT_FAMILY` + `FONT_SIZE`), a fully-custom typography
281:   (`Font.custom(name, size, weight, design)` → all four axes), or a system
282:   size/weight/design (`Font.system(size, weight, design)`). `TextStyle` is the
283:   design-system typography enum (`TEXT_STYLE` codes). The individual font
284:   modifiers (`FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `FontFamily`, `FontDesign`,
285:   `FontStyle`, `FontWidth`, `Italic`) remain available for one-off overrides.
286: - **Value types**: `ValueTypes.forProperty` mirrors `value_type_for` —
287:   `COLOR` family → `COLOR`; `VISIBLE`/`ENABLED`/`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`/`UNDERLINE`/
288:   `STRIKETHROUGH`/`COLOR_INVERT`/`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`/`IS_SECURE`/
289:   `IS_INDETERMINATE`/`FIXED_SIZE_*`/`SELECTED` → `U8`; `LINE_LIMIT`/`SELECTION`/
290:   `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BORDER_EDGES` → `U32`;
291:   `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` → `STRING`; enum-valued
292:   properties ride as `F32` holding the numeric enum code. `FontWeight` uses the
293:   spec's numeric 100–900 scale.
294: - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
295:   `untracked` — glitch-free synchronous flush, equality suppression,
296:   circular-dependency detection. The `Scheduler`'s global effect queue is
297:   **thread-safe** (all entry points synchronized) so a request/SSR-thread flush can
298:   never race the actor's mid-flush mutation of another session's pending effects.
299:   An effect that **throws during a flush is not permanently unsubscribed**: its
300:   pre-run producer edges are restored, so it retries on the next dependency change
301:   (a transient error can't silently kill a node's binding).
302: - **Emitter** (`emit`): mounts once, stable ids, node-level binding effects
303:   (a signal change re-emits only that node), `FrameOpcodeSink` /
304:   `RingOpcodeSink`. **`Signals.constant` / `ConstantSignal`**: a view or
305:   modifier holds one `Signal<T>` per reactive value (the raw `of(T)` overload is
306:   sugar for a constant); the emitter treats a constant as a plain, non-reactive
307:   property (no binding/effect).
308: - **Structural reactivity** (spec DSL.md §3.4): `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>,
309:   then, else)` and `when(Signal<T>, Case.of(...)...) / Case.otherwise(...)` —
310:   statically importable lowercase factories on a final class (mirrors
311:   `Signals`; `if`/`switch`/`case`/`else` are Java keywords). A structural
312:   container materializes as a `Group` slot (bare `VSTACK` node); the emitter's
313:   structural effect reconciles the slot's single child on selector change —
314:   position+type-stable ids, `TREE` deltas only, identical recompute emits
315:   **zero** opcodes, nested containers work, and the slot's subtree owns its own
316:   bindings. `RenderResult` routing maps are now live unmodifiable views (a swap
317:   updates tap/text/value/date routing after mount).
318: - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.router`, spec DSL.md §4.5): `Route` (absolute
319:   path, `pathOnly()` strips query/fragment), `RouteTable` (literal + `:param`
320:   patterns, guards → `replace()` redirect, `fallback` 404), `Router`
321:   (`Signal<Route>` + back-stack; `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace`/`back`,
322:   `handlePlatformNavigation`/`handleEvent`), **`Navigation`** (the ergonomic
323:   facade: `Navigation.navigator(initialPath).route(...).fallback(...).build()`
324:   collapses table + router + seeding, `Navigation.container(router)` is the slot,
325:   `Navigation.isActive(router, path)` → a reactive `Signal<Boolean>` for
326:   active-route styling, `Navigation.ROUTER` = the `EnvironmentKey<Router>`),
327:   **`Params`** (typed path-param access — `get`/
328:   `intValue`/`longValue`/`doubleValue`/`booleanValue`/`path` — replacing the raw
329:   `Map` in `RouteHandler`), **a bound router** (`Navigation.navigator()...
330:   .build(WritableSignal<String>)` — the router binds to the host-provided
331:   `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal: external writes are re-routed **guard-aware**,
332:   its own navigation is mirrored back, the initial value is guard-processed), and
333:   **generic scoped environment values**
334:   (`EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` + the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value
335:   (`environmentBinding(e -> e.key(key).value(value))`) +
336:   `Environment.value(key)` — the `.environment` style, hierarchical nearest-
337:   wins; a `NavigationContainer` scopes `Navigation.ROUTER` to its destination
338:   subtree and structural slots re-apply the incoming scope on re-render via
339:   `PathlandNode.environmentForChildren`/`Emitter.reconcileSlot`; **reads always
340:   return a signal** — `Environment.value(key)` → `Signal<T>`, a value injected as
341:   a `Signal` comes back as the same instance (bindable for reactive updates) and a
342:   plain value is wrapped in a constant signal; a read made before the key is bound
343:   returns a **lazy signal** that captures the binding on the first `.get()` during
344:   render, enabling the `@Environment` **field style**
345:   (`private final Signal<Router> router = Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER);`)),
346:   plus the
347:   **universal active platform path** (`Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` =
348:   `EnvironmentKey<String>`, the host injects a writable signal — provided for every
349:   app with or without navigation — read via `Environment.value` and observed via
350:   the `PathChange` modifier value (`pathChange(p -> p.listener(...))`) /
351:   reading the signal; fires on every change incl.
352:   the initial value),
353:   `NavigationContainer` (structural
354:   slot emitting the `ROUTE` property coalesced into the same frame as the
355:   destination swap, plus a `NAV_DEPTH` U32 back-stack-depth property
356:   (`router.depth()` = stack size + 1; `push`+1 / `pop`−1 / `replace` unchanged)
357:   so native navigation adapters reconcile their page stack by depth, a
358:   `NAV_CHROME` chrome-mode property (`Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT` / `Chrome.CUSTOM`
359:   — the renderer supplies default navigation chrome, or the developer owns all
360:   nav UI), and a `TRANSITION` PlatformDefault hint renderers may use
361:   to animate the swap), `NavigationLink` (a `BUTTON` that pushes — both
362:   explicit-router and **router-agnostic** overloads). **Any component can change
363:   the route** (spec DSL.md §4.5): `Button.make(b -> …).modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate/push/replace(path))`
364:   (`NavigationIntent`) and router-agnostic
365:   `NavigationLink.make(l -> l.label("..").to(path))` record a
366:   `NavOp` intent on the node; the emitter resolves it to the **nearest
367:   enclosing** `Router` (the `NavigationContainer` the component lives under)
368:   during the retained-tree walk and exposes it on
369:   `RenderResult.navigateActions` (a live `node id → Runnable` map like
370:   `tapActions`), which the host routes on tap before `tapActions`. The route is a
371:   **plain signal** (not persisted; the URL is the web's persistence layer) and
372:   the host **seeds it before mount** via `navigate(...)` — no `Location`, no
373:   environment-carried route. A `NAVIGATE` event (`Event.navigate(url)` /
374:   `Event.navigateBack()`, wire round-trip via `FrameCodec`) routes into the
375:   router through `RenderResult.navigateHandler`.
376: - **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
377:   both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
378:   `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets), and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`**
379:   (`isEnvironment`/`decodeEnvironment` → `EnvironmentData` — the platform
380:   environment: viewport + initial route; SSR synthesizes it from the request,
381:   the DOM client sends/enriches it over the WebSocket).
382: - **JNA ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI;
383:   `PathlandCore.ringMut(handle)` borrows the underlying ring for the in-process
384:   GTK renderer (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`), and `RingOpcodeSink` is the zero-copy
385:   guest writer.
386: - **Input dispatch** (`emit.InputDispatcher`): routes raw `EVENT`s into the
387:   `RenderResult` registries (tap / navigate / text / value / date, `NAVIGATE`
388:   URL → active path, back → router). Shared by the server session
389:   (`PathlandSession.dispatch`) and the native GTK host, so both route events
390:   identically and neither reaches into view internals.
391: - **`BINDING_ID` on the ring path**: for a `RingOpcodeSink`, the emitter sets
392:   `BINDING_ID` (= the node's id) on every text/value/date-bound control so the
393:   GTK renderer's transport-aware event guard fires (`TEXT_CHANGED` /
394:   `VALUE_CHANGED`). The frame (SSR) path never emits it, keeping server output
395:   unchanged.
396: - **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
397:   `pathland-view-processor`.
398: - **Design tokens**: `Color` is `(argb, token)` — `Color.token("color.primary")`
399:   (incl. `dark.*` paths) usable in every color-taking modifier
400:   (`ForegroundStyle`/`Background`/`Border`/`Tint`, and the `Color` view). The
401:   emitter sends token refs as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (path in the frame's
402:   string section / arena) in both `FrameOpcodeSink` and `RingOpcodeSink`
403:   (spec/TOKENS.md).
404: - **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: `Theme` — single-value
405:   builders (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme(light,
406:   dark)` composes a light + dark pair. Both implement the `ThemeData` interface
407:   (`emit`/`emitInto`); `Theme.emit`/`AdaptiveTheme.emit` write one frame of
408:   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides (the dark theme's with the `dark.` prefix),
409:   and `OpcodeSink.setDesignToken` puts path + STRING values into the string
410:   section (frame) / arena (ring). The `Emitter` takes a `ThemeData` and rides it
411:   into the mount + resync frames. Overrides are renderer-global — they never
412:   re-emit nodes.
413: 
414: ## Not implemented / gaps
415: 
416: - `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` are usable as modifiers (`actionId`/`bindingId`); the
417:   Java model routes events by node id through the emitter's registries
418:   (`RenderResult`), so the frame (SSR) path does not set them automatically.
419:   On the ring (desktop) path the emitter auto-sets `BINDING_ID` for bound
420:   controls (see Implemented) — the GTK renderer gates value/text events on it.
421: - Structural reconcile does not emit `SET_PROPERTY` for a *removed* property on
422:   a matched node (the wire has no unset; the renderer keeps the last value) —
423:   consistent with the Rust engine.
424: 
425: ## Verified by
426: 
427: `mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
428: state, structural-reactivity (`ConditionalTest`) and the router (`RouterTest`:

432: intents** (`.navigate/.push/.replace` + router-agnostic `NavigationLink`

434: **`Navigation` facade / `Params` / `isActive`**, the **scoped environment
435: values** (`View.environment` + `Environment.value` hierarchy/restore), and the
436: **universal active path** (a bound router re-routing guard-aware on external
437: signal writes + mirroring its own navigation; `onPathChange` firing on changes));
438: the JNA ring
439: test runs when `libpathland_core` is on `java.library.path`. The v2 authoring

1: # pathland-view (Rust DSL) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 9, 2026
4: 
5: The SwiftUI-style **view DSL** (`no_std`) building `pathland_engine::Node`
6: trees. Protocol contract: `spec/`, authoring surface: `spec/DSL.md`.
7: 
8: ## Implemented
9: 
10: - **The three authoring operations** (spec/DSL.md §2): every concrete view
11:   exposes **values** (`Type::with(|c| …)` static / `view.with(|c| …)` chained),
12:   **modifiers** (`Type::modifiers((A, B))` / `view.modifiers((A, B))`, single or
13:   tuple list) and, for content-bearing views, **children**
14:   (`Type::children(vec![…])` / `view.children(vec![…])`). The three may be used
15:   at creation or chained, in any order.
16: - **Per-view `Config`** (`TextConfig`, `StackConfig`, `GridConfig`,
17:   `RangeConfig`, …) with fluent setters, consumed by the value builders. Values
18:   move structural properties (`spacing`/`alignment`/grid counts) into the config
19:   (no longer modifiers).
20: - **Views**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`,
21:   `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`,
22:   `Icon` (semantic symbols via `IconName` + `icon(…)`), `Image` (sets
23:   `IMAGE_SOURCE`), `Color` (dual identity: a layout-greedy View *and* a value
24:   passed into style modifiers), `Shape` + named `Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/
25:   `Ellipse`, `Divider`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Toggle`, `Slider`,
26:   `TextField` (sets `PROMPT`), `TextEditor`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`,
27:   `Menu`, `ColorPicker` (+ the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros and
28:   `text`/`spacer`/`button`/`icon`/`image` free functions).
29: - **Modifiers** (decoupled values applied via `modifiers(...)`): `Padding`,
30:   `FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `Font(Font)`, `FontFamily`, `FontDesign` (the enum
31:   *is* the modifier), `ForegroundStyle` (no `.color()`), `Background`, `Border`,
32:   `Tint`, `Frame`, `Opacity`, `Hidden`, `CornerRadius`, `LineLimit`,
33:   `TextAlignment`, `TruncationMode`, `Offset`, `Position`, `ZIndex`,
34:   `PointerEvents`, `TapGesture` (`TapGesture::new(f)`).
35: - **No `Mod` suffix**: modifiers are named for the modifier they apply;
36:   `FontDesignMod` is gone (`FontDesign` is the modifier).
37: - **Typography** (`Font` + `TextStyle`): `Font::large_title()`…`caption2()` emit
38:   the predefined `TEXT_STYLE` (renderer-owned size/weight); `Font::custom(name,
39:   size)`, `Font::system(size)`, `Font::system_weight(size, weight)`, and
40:   `Font::custom_full(name, size, weight, design)` emit the raw
41:   `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_DESIGN` axes.
42: - **`Frame` infinity**: infinite `width`/`height` hints (`f32::INFINITY`,
43:   SwiftUI `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) normalize to the `size::FILL`
44:   sentinel on emission.
45: - **Composition**: blanket `ViewExt::modifiers` + `ViewModifier` for custom
46:   modifiers; `Modified<V>` wrapper (applies its modifier list at `build`).
47:   `Modified<V>` implements `Configurable`/`Children` (delegating) so the three
48:   operations are order-independent.
49: - **Alignment enum** (`Align`): Leading/Center/Trailing.
50: - **Design tokens**: `Color` is `Literal(u32)` | `Token(&'static str)` —
51:   `Color::token("color.primary")` (and `dark.*` paths) usable as a View and in
52:   every color-taking modifier; token refs emit as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type
53:   via `Node::token_properties` (spec/TOKENS.md).
54: - **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: re-exports
55:   `pathland_engine::Theme` and `AdaptiveTheme { light, dark }`. Emit once at
56:   mount via `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.
57: - **Reactive signals (Phase 1)**: a shared `Runtime`
58:   (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local) with typed handles
59:   (`Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>`, `SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`), value
60:   signals, **computed** (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and
61:   **effect** (runs immediately, then on dependency change) signals, and
62:   `untracked` reads; `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. The DSL
63:   binds a node's **text** (`Text::with(|t| { t.text_signal(sig); })`) and a
64:   **property** — **every value member accepts a raw value or a signal**
65:   (`Reactive<T>`/`IntoReactive<T>`, spec DSL.md §2): a signal is a node-level
66:   binding, so a change re-emits only that node's `SET_PROPERTY`. Modifiers spell
67:   this `Padding(16.0)` (static) vs `Padding(sig)` (bound) — `FontSize(sig)`,
68:   `ForegroundStyle(sig)`, `Background(sig)`, `Opacity(sig)`,
69:   `Border::new(color, width)`, `CornerRadius(sig)`, `FontWeight(sig)`,
70:   `LineLimit(sig)`, `Offset::new(x, y)`, `Position::new(x, y)`, `ZIndex(sig)` …
71:   the former `Bound`/`*.bound` modifier surface is **removed**. View configs
72:   take signals the same way (`VStack::with(|v| { v.spacing(sig); })`, «Grid»:
73:   `columns`/`rows`/`spacing`, `ProgressView::value`, `Gauge` value/min/max).
74:   Reactive values cover the engine's `SignalValueKind`s (`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/
75:   `bool`); `Align` and token colors remain static (no typed signal kind yet).
76: - **Two-way bindings + actions (Phase 2)**: a control binds a writable signal
77:   and records an app-side **input sink** (a `Gesture::TextInput`/`ValueInput`/
78:   `DateInput` on the node, never serialized) plus the `BINDING_ID` event gate —
79:   `TextField`/`TextEditor` (`t.text(sig)`), `Toggle` (`t.is_on(sig)`),
80:   `Slider`/`Stepper` (`s.bind(sig)`, initial from the signal), `Picker`
81:   (`p.bind(sig)`). `Button::action(f)` wires the tap. A host collects the sinks
82:   with `collect_input_handlers` and routes `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED`/
83:   `DATE_CHANGED` into them (the sink writes the signal; the host re-emits the
84:   tree to flush the delta).
85: - **Styles + environment (Phase 3)**: an [`Environment`] threaded through
86:   `View::build_env` (the `no_std` equivalent of the Java thread-local) scopes a
87:   subtree; `ButtonStyle` (`make_body(&ButtonConfig) -> Option<Box<dyn View>>`)
88:   supplies a button's content (Composite Override Mode), applied with
89:   `ViewExt::button_style(style)`. Built-ins `PlainButtonStyle` (native path) and
90:   `BorderedButtonStyle`; custom styles implement the trait.
91: - **Structural reactivity + navigation (Phase 4)**: `Conditional::when(signal,
92:   then, else)` builds the selected branch (the host rebuilds + re-emits; the
93:   engine reconciles into `TREE` deltas). Navigation: `Params` + `RouteTable`
94:   (`/users/:id` matching + fallback), `Router` (path signal + back-stack:
95:   `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace`), `NavigationContainer` (builds the current
96:   destination and carries `ROUTE`/`NAV_DEPTH`/`NAV_CHROME` on a container slot),
97:   and `NavigationLink` (a button that changes the route via a router).
98: - **Media (Phase 6)**: `Video` — the video playback **surface**
99:   (`Video::new(Rc<MediaController>)` / `video(rc)`) referencing a
100:   `pathland_engine::MediaController`; `MediaControllerExt::attach()` on a
101:   controller (`Rc`) is the **non-visual marker** that materializes its
102:   `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node with the transport bound (`MEDIA_SOURCE` as a reactive
103:   STRING binding, `PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/
104:   `MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE` as property bindings). `assign_ids` pins the
105:   controller's id and links each surface's `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`. A **`VideoStyle`**
106:   (`ViewExt::video_style`) supplies the surface's control content — the style reads
107:   the surface's controller through `VideoStyleConfig` — while the default
108:   `NativeVideoStyle` keeps the surface a leaf with renderer-native controls.
109:   **Audio has no view** — bind ordinary views to the controller's signals.
110: - **Persisted state (Phase 5)**: `pathland_view::state` — a platform-neutral
111:   `StateStore` trait (`get`/`set` by key over `SignalValue`) + the in-process
112:   `InMemoryStateStore`; `PersistentState::state(name, initial)` returns a
113:   `State<T>` that auto-loads (or the initial) and auto-saves on change (via a

questions.question: The issue is that a full-snapshot `SIZE_THAT_FITS` emission can carry duplicate node ids when a `View` instance is reused across candidates (each copy of a shared subtree is materialized per candidate; identity-stable nodes like a media controller re-introduce the same id). You noted the developer maybe shouldn't be able to reuse a View instance at all. Which approach should the plan take?

options.label: Reject View reuse in SizeThatFits (Recommended)
options.description: Fail loudly (IllegalStateException) if the same View instance is passed to more than one candidate, plus the no-duplicate-id frame guard. Enforces the spec invariant at the authoring surface rather than silently cloning shared state.

options.label: Only add the no-duplicate-id guard
options.description: Keep reuse allowed; make assignIds the single id authority so every candidate copy gets distinct ids, and add a debug_assert/test guard. Reuse stays legal but is 'make it work', not 'make it impossible'.

options.label: Deep-clone reused views per candidate
options.description: Allow reuse but render an independent deep copy per candidate so shared internal state (State fields, controllers) is never shared across branches. More invasive to the DSL.

content.text:
I've completed my research. Here's the plan.

## Context (what I found)

- On `main`, the Java emitter's `assignIds` is the *only* place ordinary node ids are handed out (`node.id = nextId++` in `Emitter.java`), and `render()` already produces a fresh `PathlandNode` subtree per candidate, so a shared `View` reused across `SizeThatFits` candidates **already gets distinct ids today**. The duplicate-id corruption the issue describes is only *reintroduced* by a later pass that overrides an id after `assignIds` — the media-controller "pinned id" (which lives on the `spec/media-controller` branch, not `main`).
- There is no spec invariant ("a frame's node ids are unique") and no emitter guard. So the real gaps on `main` are: (a) the invariant is unstated, (b) nothing fails loudly if it's violated, and (c) the authoring surface lets a developer hand the *same* `View` instance to two candidates.

## Plan

### 1. Spec first
- **`spec/OPCODE.md` §Frame Lifecycle** — add the invariant: a frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id; `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes reference each id for exactly one node.
- **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §SizeThatFits** — document that in a full-snapshot emission a shared subtree is materialized once per candidate and **every copy gets a distinct id** (no id reused between candidates, including identity-stable nodes).

### 2. Emitter: single id authority + no-duplicate-id guard (`Emitter.java`)
- Keep `assignIds`/`nextId` as the sole id source; add a `private static boolean hasDuplicateIds(PathlandNode)` helper (walks the retained tree, detects a repeated id via a set).
- Invoke it as a fail-loud guard at mount, `renderFull`, and after each structural reconcile, throwing `IllegalStateException` on a duplicate (so any future id-overriding pass — media pinning — trips it loudly). Tests call the same helper directly.

### 3. Reject `View` instance reuse in `SizeThatFits` (your chosen approach)
- In `SizeThatFits.make(...)` (both `Fit...` and `View...` overloads), detect when the **same `View` instance is used as the candidate of more than one `Fit`** (reference identity on `Fit.view()`) and throw `IllegalStateException` with a clear message ("a View instance can be used in at most one SizeThatFits candidate; create a fresh instance per candidate").
- Scope: this rejects `SizeThatFits.make(Fit.of(shared), Fit.of(shared))`. It does **not** reject a view shared as a *subtree inside* two distinct candidate roots (the music player's `mainArea` pattern), which is the legitimate reuse and already yields unique ids.

### 4. Tests (`SizeThatFitsTest.java`, `pathland-view`)
- Snapshot emission with two candidates that share a subtree (an ordinary view) → assert every `CREATE_NODE`/`SET_*` id across the whole frame is unique, with and without an identity-stable node (a fake pinned-id node stands in for the media controller, since media isn't on `main`).
- `SizeThatFits.make` throws when the same instance is passed to two candidates.
- Guard helper: a hand-built `PathlandNode` tree with a repeated id → `hasDuplicateIds` detects it (the "fails loudly" proof).

### 5. status.md + build
- Update `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` (guard + reject-reuse rule) and `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/status.md` (Rust `assign_ids` already reserves pinned ids; note the invariant). 
- Verify: `cd lib/java && mvn install` (the `pathland-view` module at minimum) and `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.

### Notes / one thing to confirm
- The issue says "start from `main` on a fresh branch" — I'll branch `fix/size-that-fits-unique-ids` from `main` (per the issue), not the current `spec/media-controller` branch. I won't commit unless you ask.
- Rust's `SizeThatFits` only ever emits one selected child (no full-snapshot emission), so the reject-reuse surface and the duplicate-id scenario are Java/SSR-only today; I'll add the Rust `assign_ids` uniqueness note only.

Two quick confirmations before I start:
1. Do you want the reject-reuse error to also cover a `View` instance shared **inside** two distinct candidates (i.e. force the demo's `mainArea` to be a factory/lambda rather than a reused instance), or is rejecting same-instance-as-two-candidates sufficient for now?
2. Branch from `main` as `fix/size-that-fits-unique-ids` — OK?

Plan finalized. Both open questions resolved: reject-reuse scope = same instance as two candidates only; branch `fix/size-that-fits-unique-ids` from `main`.

## Final plan

**1. Spec**
- `spec/OPCODE.md` §Frame Lifecycle: add the invariant — a frame MUST NOT contain two nodes with the same id; `TREE`/`PARAMETER` reference each id for exactly one node.
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §SizeThatFits: full-snapshot emission materializes a shared subtree once per candidate; every copy gets a **distinct** id, no reuse between candidates (including identity-stable nodes).

**2. `Emitter.java` (single id authority + fail-loud guard)**
- Keep `assignIds`/`nextId` the sole id source.
- Add `private static boolean hasDuplicateIds(PathlandNode)` (tree walk, set-based).
- Call it at mount, `renderFull`, and after each structural reconcile; throw `IllegalStateException` on a duplicate.

**3. `SizeThatFits.java` (reject reuse)**
- In both `make(...)` overloads, reject the same `View` instance used as more than one candidate (reference identity on `Fit.view()`) with a clear `IllegalStateException`. Subtree-level sharing (the music player's `mainArea`) stays allowed.

**4. Tests (`SizeThatFitsTest.java`)**
- Snapshot emission, two candidates sharing a subtree → assert every node id across the whole frame is unique (with and without a fake identity-stable pinned-id node, since media isn't on `main`).
- `make(...)` throws on same-instance-two-candidates.
- `hasDuplicateIds` detects a hand-built duplicate-id tree (the "fails loudly" proof).

**5. status.md + verification**
- Update `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` and `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/status.md`.
- Verify: `cd lib/java && mvn install` (or the `pathland-view` module) and `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.

No commit unless you ask. Ready to implement on your go-ahead.

768: ### ProxyView — `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E
769: 
770: A **proxy view**: a transparent container whose child subtree is served by a
771: **different Pathland server**. It lets one app compose views from several
772: servers into a single unified document. The proxying server (the app that owns
773: the proxy node) connects to the origin server as a Pathland **host** (client),
774: receives the origin's subtree, and splices it into its own stream.
775: 
776: - **Protocol**: a container node with **exactly one** child in the live form —
777:   the origin subtree's root. The origin subtree's nodes are ordinary nodes of
778:   the same protocol; the proxying server has **remapped their node ids** into a
779:   disjoint high range so they never collide with the proxying app's own ids.
780: - **Layout**: a **transparent passthrough** container. It imposes no spacing or
781:   alignment of its own; it proposes its own allocated size to its single child
782:   and, unless the app constrains it (`frame`/size modifiers), sizes to that
783:   child. Renderers render it as a plain container (a box/`div`) — there is no
784:   proxy-specific native element.
785: - **Events**: raw events whose target id falls in a proxy's remapped range are
786:   the origin server's; the proxying server forwards them (id remapped back) to
787:   the origin over the origin connection rather than dispatching them locally.

789:   child subtree belongs to the origin server's retained tree. The proxying app
790:   never diffs the origin subtree — it forwards the origin's deltas verbatim
791:   (id-remapped). A **full-snapshot** (`META::RESYNC`) of the proxying app embeds
792:   the origin's current snapshot; the origin snapshot is requested with a

256:     private static int slotByThreshold(RenderResult result, ProtocolFrame frame, float threshold) {
257:         for (int id : result.fitInputs().keySet()) {
258:             Opcode query = frame.opcodes().stream()
259:                     .filter(o -> o.category() == Categories.PARAMETER
260:                             && o.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY
261:                             && o.a() == id && (o.b() & 0xFFFF) == Properties.FIT_QUERY)
262:                     .findFirst().orElseThrow();
263:             byte[] strings = frame.strings();
264:             int offset = query.c();
265:             int count = le32(strings, offset);
266:             for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
267:                 if (Float.intBitsToFloat(le32(strings, offset + 4 + i * 4)) == threshold) {
268:                     return id;
269:                 }
270:             }
271:         }
272:         throw new AssertionError("no slot with threshold " + threshold);
273:     }

input.newString:
- **`SizeThatFits` fit slot** (`SizeThatFits.make(Fit...)` + `Fit.of(view, minWidth)`):
  a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
  thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
  The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
  (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
  the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
  value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
  (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
  state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
  slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
  with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
  the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
  controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
  compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
  unchanged width). The **web-SSR full-snapshot emission** (issue #141) is an
  internal emitter mode (`Emitter.snapshotEmission(true)`, armed by
  `PathlandSession`): on mount/resync the slot emits EVERY candidate in `FIT_QUERY`
  order so the SSR renders all branches gated by CSS container queries (a no-JS
  correct first paint) — the authored DSL is unchanged. `PathlandNode.fitReported`
  gates the mount-time structural effect so the multi-candidate presentation is
  not collapsed before the renderer reports; the first `FIT_CHANGED` (recorded
  before the incoming index) downgrades the slot to the single selected child via
  the normal reconcile, and the web client unwraps the gated branches. The
  downgrade is a **clean N→1**: it keeps the SELECTED candidate's node as-is
  (retaining its id + subtree, zero churn) and removes the others — it never
  positionally diffs, because both candidates are frequently the same component
  and morphing the loser's node into the winner would relocate the winner into
  the SSR's loser wrapper and break the renderer's candidate-position CSS gate.
  **View reuse** (issue #159): the same `View` instance may not be the candidate
  of two `Fit`s — `SizeThatFits.make` rejects it (`IllegalStateException`), since
  it would be materialized once per candidate and leak shared state / ids.
  Sharing a subtree **inside** two distinct candidate roots stays allowed; every
  materialized copy gets a distinct node id. The emitter enforces the frame's
  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle) with
  `Emitter.duplicateIds` / a fail-loud guard at mount, resync, and after each
  structural reconcile, so an id-overriding pass (an identity-stable node pinning
  a playback key) can never silently corrupt an id-keyed consumer.

  pinned**: a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node keeps the id it was first given, so a
  structural swap that shifts other ids never changes the playback key; the same

  **unique-node-id invariant** (spec/OPCODE.md §Frame Lifecycle): a frame never
  carries two nodes with the same id.

Add unique-id invariant to spec/OPCODE.md and SizeThatFits note to spec/PRIMITIVES.md
Add no-duplicate-id guard to Emitter.java (single id authority)

content.text:
Implemented issue #159 on `fix/size-that-fits-unique-ids` (from `main`).

## Changes

**Spec**
- `spec/OPCODE.md` §Frame Lifecycle: added the **unique node-id invariant** (a frame never has two nodes with the same id; every materialized copy gets a distinct id).
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §SizeThatFits: documented shared-subtree full-snapshot materialization — one copy per candidate, each with a distinct id.

**Emitter** (`lib/java/pathland-view`)
- `Emitter.duplicateIds(PathlandNode)` — public tree-scan helper returning repeated ids.
- `guardUniqueIds()` — fail-loud `IllegalStateException` at mount, `renderFull` (resync), and after each structural reconcile. `assignIds`/`nextId` remains the single id authority.
- `SizeThatFits.make(...)` now rejects the **same `View` instance as the candidate of two `Fit`s** (`IllegalStateException`), preventing shared mutable state/ids from being materialized twice. Sharing a subtree *inside* distinct candidate roots stays allowed (music-player pattern).

**Tests** (`SizeThatFitsTest`, now 11)
- Snapshot with a shared subtree → all `CREATE_NODE` ids unique.
- A cached `PathlandNode` reused across candidates trips the guard loudly (the media-pin analog).
- `duplicateIds` detects a hand-built duplicate tree.
- Both `make` overloads reject same-instance candidates.

**Status**
- Updated `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` and `lib/rust/crates/pathland-engine/status.md`.

## Verification
- `mvn -pl pathland-view -am test` — green (157).
- `mvn -pl pathland-demo-views -am test` — green.
- `mvn -pl pathland-server-core -am test` — green (incl. SSR + proxy integration).
- `cargo test` (workspace) — green.

Note: the first render-html run failed on a stale Rust dylib; after `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` it passed. No commit made.
